en: Oṃ, homage to the glorious Mahāvairocana Vajrasattva! Homage to the glorious Satguru!
Oṃ, homage to the Three Jewels! Oṃ, homage to all the glorious Buddhas and Bodhisattvas!
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Noble and Glorious Mahāpratyamgirā.
O you who possess the fresh, dark-blue luster that causes the proclamation of all the auspicious and peerless qualities of the illustrious Yamadviṣa!
I bow with my mind to the one who holds a vajra, sword, and discus in his hands, and carries a knife, lotus, and skull-cup.
Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Trāyastriṃśa gods in the Nandana grove, together with all the gods.
Jewels, gold, the Śivaraśāṣāra tree, and the Vanaspati tree.

It was adorned with various kinds of plants, creepers, lotuses, utpalas, karṇikāras, blue water-lilies, tilakas, aśokas, māndāras, kuvalayas, campakas, nāgapuṣpas, and so forth; it was beautifully decorated with wish-fulfilling trees (kalpavṛkṣas).

Adorned with various ornaments, resounding with the warbling of flocks of various birds such as deer, filled with the thundering of drums, kettledrums, and great drums, and made to sport in manifold ways by Indra and the gods such as Śakra and Brahmā, along with divine apsarases— the entire Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha.
Through the empowerment of the bodhisattvas.
Together with all the gods, beginning with Śakra and Brahmā, as well as the Vidyādharas, gods, and Apsarases.
The Bodhisattva always recited this Vidyā-mantra for the Blessed One, the Great Sage, twenty-one times.
Accompanied by eight hundred thousand times ten million followers, as follows:
To the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Apratibhāna.
To the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Vipulaśrī.
To the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Samantaśrī.
To the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Anantaśrī.
To the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Sumantaśrī.
To the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Kamalaśrī.
To the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Mahāmatiśrī.
To the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Divākaraśrī.
To the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Vividhaśrī.
To the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Aśeṣaśrī.
To the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Mañjuśrī.
To the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Vajrahastaśrī.
To the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Cakrahastaśrī.
To the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Samantaśrī.
Thus, with these as their leaders, there were infinite and boundless assemblies of irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
Honored, revered, worshipped, and highly esteemed by the great.
In the midst of the assembly, Mahāpratyamgira is seated upon a lotus throne.
He has attained the meditative absorption of the arrangement of all the Tathāgatas.
He entered the meditative absorption named "The Uṣṇīṣa Survey."
Immediately thereafter, the great bodhisattva named Vimokṣatā emerged from the three continuums of the lower realms.

He emits from the tuft of hair between his brows a multitude of garlands of radiating light rays. This is the opening statement of all the scriptures, which restates the author; for it was indeed spoken by the Blessed One while in the state of a Bodhisattva, not having yet attained direct realization [of Buddhahood].
By that, the trichiliocosm great thousandfold world system was illuminated.
By that radiance, all sentient beings were liberated from the bonds of the afflictions within their minds.
Having individually reached those who had attained joy, he illuminated them on all sides.
Having worshipped with clouds of various offerings.

Hundreds of thousands of gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, kumbhāṇḍas, apsarases, and other human and non-human beings, having circumambulated [the Blessed One] and bowed their heads in homage,
[praised] the Blessed Ones, the Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣasītāntapattrā Nānāparājitās.
Mahāpratyamgirā, having previously seated herself upon a pure throne, spoke thus:
Oh, the Buddha! Oh, the Buddha! How beautiful is the Dharma of the Buddha! It is for the sake of that very purpose.
And our great vow is the establishment of the practice of awakening.
Then the Blessed One [was attended] by five hundred monks and the five mothers.
Together with a great host of bodhisattvas, at that time, along with the Samyak-kalpas.
The sons of the gods were attending upon the Blessed One.
Then, indeed, from the Bhagavat Buddha-sattva, the jewel-mantra syllables issued forth from the circle of hair between his brows.

Oṃ, homage to the Buddha! Oṃ, homage to the Dharma! Oṃ, homage to the Saṅgha! Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Aparimitaguṇapratibhānavyūhātītakalpa! Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One Guṇaratnavyūha!
To the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śrīkalpa.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Śrīsahasreśvarameghagarjita-pratibhānavyuha.

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Sūryottamavyūhaprabhāsaśrītejorāja. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha who has brought forth awakening through oceans of incalculable millions of kalpas.

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śubhakanakavyūhaśrītejornirbhāsa. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Sarvadharmatāvikurvitashrirāja.
Thus, having offered praise to these deities and Buddhas, headed by the Blessed One.
Having paid homage, one should recite: *Oṃ namo buddhāya*.
Oṃ, homage to the Dharma. Oṃ, homage to the Saṅgha.
Oṃ, homage to all the Śrī Buddhas and Bodhisattvas!
The glorious one, who is equal to Śrī herself, bestows upon everyone the arising of all prosperity and success.
The various misfortunes of existence are summoned like a wish-fulfilling gem.
In this very context, the contact with the means of accomplishment was previously proclaimed by the venerable teacher Ariha.
However, for those who take no delight in prolixity, a concise presentation is shown.
Herein indeed is the Aparājitā Mahāpratyamgirā named Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣasītāntapattrā.

O Great Queen of Vidyās, O King of the Three Samayas, in the mantra-maṇḍala—having obtained the authority through the ritual procedure for the great-souled one who possesses the vows and commitments of the mantra and its practice: homage to the seven crores of perfectly awakened Buddhas; Oṃ, homage to the Bodhisattvas headed by Maitreya.
To the great beings, to the community of disciples, and to the Arhats in the world, I pay homage.

Homage to those who have attained heat. Homage to those who return once more. Homage to those who have gone rightly in the world. Homage to those who have entered the right path. Homage to the divine seers.
Homage to those capable of bestowing grace upon supplicants! Homage to the perfected ones and the holders of vidyā!
Homage to the divine Brahmā! Homage to Indra! Homage to the Blessed Lord Rudra! Homage to him who is accompanied by Umāpati!

Homage to the Blessed One, Nārāyaṇa! Homage to him who is saluted by the five great mudrās! Homage to the Blessed One, Mahākāla! To him who causes the city of Tripura to tremble! To him who dwells in the great cremation grounds with resolute faith! Homage to the Blessed One, who is saluted by the host of Mothers! Homage!
Homage to her who is worshipped by all the gods; homage to the Blessed One, who is honored by all the gods.
Homage to the Blessed One of the Tathāgata family! Homage to the Blessed One of the Maṇi family! Homage to the Blessed Lady of the Rāga family!
Homage to the Blessed Lady of the family of hatred! Homage to the Blessed Lady of the family of delusion!

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Dṛḍhaśūraṇasyena-praharaṇarāja. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Amitābha. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat Akṣobhya.

To the Perfectly Awakened One: Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Awakened One, Vajradharasāgaragarjita. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and [Perfectly Awakened One], Bhaikṣyarājyarājaguru Vaidūryaprabhaketurāja.
To the Perfectly Enlightened One.

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Supuṣpitasādendrarāja, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Padmottararāja.

To the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vipaśyin, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śikhin, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Viśvabhū.

To the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Krakucchanda, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Kanakamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Kāśyapa...

To the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnacandra, the Arhat...

To the Perfectly Enlightened One: Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Enlightened One, Ratnaketurāja. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Enlightened One, Samantabhadra.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Vairocana, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened Buddha.

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, King of the Fragrance-Standard of the Blooming Lotus. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Padmaguru, the Great Compassionate One. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Vajrapramardin.

To the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, Ratnakhacitā (Adorned with Jewels). Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnākara (Jewel-Mine).
To the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Gata; Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Nāgeśvararāja.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vīrasena.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vīranandin.

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnacandraprabha. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Amoghadarśin. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, [the Tathāgata] Ratnagarbhapramadattaśrī.

To the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Anantaśrī, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Nirmalaśrī, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Vīra.
To the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Prabhāśrī.

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śūraśrītārtha, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Brahmaprabhāśrī, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Brahmadattaśrī.

To the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Varuṇāvabhāsamakuṭaśrī, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Tattvaśrī, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha. Oṃ, homage.

Homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candraśrī. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Prabhāśrī. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Dharmaketurāja.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Buddhadharmakośamatiśrī. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Dharmadharmakośamatiśrī.

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, Saṃghakośamatiśrī. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, Ādibuddha. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One...

To the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vajradhātutathāgataśrī. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vajravajriṇī. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnavajritā. Oṃ, homage...
To the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmadhātuśrī.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Nārāyaṇaśrī.

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Kusumaśrī, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Padmojyotivikrīḍitābhijña, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata...
To the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Raśmiśrīyamerugarbha.

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Puṇyadhanavicitrā. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Dharmasmṛtiśrī. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One...
To the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Suparikīrtitanāmadheya; Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candraketudhvaja.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Vicitraśrī.

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Suvikrāntaśrī. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Puṣpavicitraśrī. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Vikrāntagāmin.

To the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Samantāvabhāsaśrī. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat [Samyaksaṃbuddha] Ratnapadmasupratiṣṭhitaśailendrarāja.

To the Perfectly Enlightened One: Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Enlightened One Vimaladattadharmashri. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Enlightened One Pratibhānashriyagata.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Sūryottamaśrītejonirbhāsa.

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Aparimitapramardanashri. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Gunaratnashri. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Dharmapratishtaraja.

To the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Prabhāvyūhasūkīrṇa. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Sahasrajyotiśrī.

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śubhakanakaśrī. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Gagananirnādavyūhaśrī. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One...
To the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, the Glory of the True Nature of All Phenomena.

Having approached and paid homage to all the Tathāgatas, I shall proclaim this *Mahāpratyamgirā*, named the Blessed One’s *Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣasitātapatrā Aparājitā*, which is worthy of salutation and worship.
And it shall be worthy of circumambulation.
Oṃ, homage to the Triple Gem! Homage! May the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, attend to me.
I go for refuge. I myself go for refuge to the Buddha; I go for refuge to the Dharma; I go for refuge to the Saṅgha.

In this way, may all those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who reside, remain, and live in as many world-systems as there are— those Blessed Ones known as the Great Aparājita Mahāpratyāṅgirā, the White-Utmost-Leaf Uṣṇīṣas of all Tathāgatas— may those Buddhas attend to me.
O Blessed Ones, it would be a supreme service: [to recite] this Aparājitā, named Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣasitātapatrā,
in this birth, in other births, and in all births throughout the cycle of existence (*saṃsāra*) until the pinnacle of existence is reached.

It would be a transgression against the cycle of existence (*saṃsāra*) for one who has committed an evil deed, or caused it to be done, or approved of its being done; or [one who has] stolen property belonging to a *stūpa* or the *Saṅgha*;
or who has stolen, or caused to be stolen, or approved of the stealing of wealth belonging to the four quarters.

Or if one has practiced by undertaking the ten unwholesome paths of action; or if one has encouraged others to undertake them, or caused others to do so in the past, or rejoiced in them—by such means there may be a karmic obstruction (*karmāvaraṇa*). Or one goes to the Avīci hell, or to the animal realm.

May I not go to this poison; may I not go to the borderlands among the people, nor be reborn among the barbarians, or among those with long lifespans; may I not fall among the gods, nor suffer from defects in my sense faculties.
One might fall into wrong view;
one might reject the appearance of a Buddha or the path to dispassion— all of that constitutes a defilement of action against those Buddhas,
the Blessed Ones, who have become wisdom and have become the standard of truth.

In the presence of those who know and see, I confess, I do not conceal, and I do not hide [my faults]. I shall undertake restraint regarding this. May the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, attend to me as I was born in this life and in other lives—throughout the succession of births while wandering in saṃsāra—[regarding] my giving.

May this Veda be given, may this instruction be given, even to one who has entered the womb; or may it be protected as a morsel of food. Whatever roots of merit I have from my practice of celibacy (*brahmacarya*), whatever roots of merit I have from surrounding sentient beings, whatever roots of merit I have from the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*), and whatever roots of merit I have from primordial wisdom (*jñāna*).
This is the root of wholesome dharmas: the Aparājitā Mahāpratyamgirā named Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣasitātapatrā.
Having gathered all that together into one mass, having hastened toward it, and having condensed it, [one should apply it] to the unsurpassed...
I dedicate [this] to supreme perfect enlightenment. Just as I dedicate it, so did the Blessed Buddhas of the past dedicate it; so will the Blessed Buddhas of the future dedicate it;
and so do the Blessed Buddhas of the present now dedicate it.
In that same way, I also dedicate [this merit].
O *Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣasitātapatrā*, named *Aparājitā*, the Great *Pratyaṅgirā*, by its power, I confess all my sins; I rejoice in all merit.

I pay homage to all the Buddhas. May supreme knowledge be mine. To those who have passed away, as well as those who remain, and those supreme Victors who are yet to come—I approach them all with a mind like a blade of grass, with palms joined in reverence. To those...
Bodhisattvas, possessing the strength of compassion, wander through the world for the benefit of sentient beings, acting as a refuge for the brave.
O protectors, protect me! I go for refuge to the Buddhas and the Bodhisattvas who are skilled in leading one away from the state of death.
Having approached and paid homage to all the deities, [I shall speak], O Blessed One, this *Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣasitātapatrā-nāmāparājitā-mahāpratyamgirā*.

Perform protection for me and my retinue against all obstacles. Perform peace and auspiciousness. Grant exemption from the four staves. Grant exemption from weapons. Grant the neutralization of poison and suffering. Grant the destruction of calamities.
May they establish the boundary and the foundation; may they live for a hundred years, rule for a hundred autumns, [for the sake of] myself and all sentient beings, svāhā!
The pacifier of all strife, quarrels, conflicts, and disputes.
Oṃ hūṃ bhrūṃ hraṃ hrīṃ ṣṭrīṃ, she who destroys all bhūtas and grahas!
Oṃ hūṃ bhrūṃ hraṃ hrīṃ ṣṭrīṃ, she who cuts through all the spells of others!
Oṃ hūṃ bhrūṃ hraṃ hrīṃ ṣṭrīṃ, she who grants protection from all untimely death!
Oṃ hūṃ bhrūṃ hraṃ hrīṃ ṣṭrīṃ, she who binds all sentient beings!

Oṃ hūṃ bhrūṃ hraṃ hrīṃ ṣṭrīṃ, the destroyer of all evil and wicked beings as well as bad dreams. Oṃ hūṃ bhrūṃ hraṃ hrīṃ ṣṭrīṃ, the annihilator of all yakṣas, rākṣasas, and grahas. Oṃ hūṃ bhrūṃ hraṃ hrīṃ ṣṭrīṃ, [the destroyer] of the eighty-four thousand...

She who brings about the destruction of thousands of seizing spirits (*graha*); *oṃ hūṃ bhrūṃ hraṃ hrīṃ ṣṭrīṃ*, she who brings about the propitiation of the twenty-eight lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*); *oṃ hūṃ bhrūṃ hraṃ hrīṃ ṣṭrīṃ*, she who wards off all enemies; *oṃ hūṃ bhrūṃ hraṃ hrīṃ ṣṭrīṃ*, [of] the twenty-eight...
The destroyer of great planetary afflictions.
Oṃ hūṃ bhrūṃ hraṃ hrīṃ ṣṭrīṃ! Protect, protect me and all sentient beings!
The warding off of sticks; the warding off of weapons; the neutralizing of poison; the destruction of poison.
Perform the binding of the boundary and the binding of the earth; provide protection, defense, possession, and preservation; grant peace and well-being, svāhā!
Now I shall proclaim this Aparājitā Mahāpratyamgirā, named Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣa-śītāntapattrā, which pacifies all strife, quarrels, conflicts, and disputes.
The warder-off of all malevolent spirits and grahas; the cutter-off of all foreign spells.
She who protects from untimely death; she who liberates all sentient beings from bondage; she who destroys all evil dreams.
It is the destroyer of all yakṣas, rākṣasas, and grahas; it is the destroyer of the eighty-four thousand grahas.
She who brings peace to the twenty-eight lunar mansions.
She who brings about the destruction of the eight great planets.
Oṃ hūṃ bhrūṃ hraṃ hrīṃ ṣṭrīṃ! Protect me and all sentient beings! May they provide protection, concealment, rescue, acceptance, guardianship, peace, and well-being.
The avoidance of punishment, the avoidance of weapons, the destruction of poison and suffering, and the eradication of disease.
May they perform the binding of the boundary and the binding of the earth for me, together with my retinue,
and for all sentient beings, svāhā!
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the White Canopy of the Uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas, named Aparājitā, the Great Pratyamgirā, the Queen of Great Vidyās,
the Thousand-Armed One.
O you with a thousand great heads! O you with hundreds of thousands of millions of eyes! O invincible, blazing Kālī, Mahākālī!
In the vast sphere of the three worlds, which is as pure as a great vajra.

May there be well-being for me, along with my retinue, and for all sentient beings. May they grant protection, concealment, rescue, preservation, acceptance, and fulfillment; may they grant peace, well-being, and security.
Avoidance of the staff, avoidance of weapons, freedom from pain, and freedom from affliction.
The binding of the boundary and the binding of the earth: protect, protect all sentient beings, svāhā!
From fear of kings, from fear of thieves, from fear of fire, from fear of water, from fear of poison, from fear of weapons,
from fear of enemies, from fear of foreign armies, from fear of famine, from fear of adversaries, and from fear of lightning.
From the fear of untimely death; from the fear of earthquakes; from the fear of royal punishment.

Tigers, lions, elephants, and bears, the suns, and all enemies [are overcome].
And all the guardians of hell, as well as the ḍākinīs and rākṣasas.
All these bondages arise from the bondage of the single mind.
And through the taming of the mind, all things become subdued.
Because all fears and immeasurable sufferings [arise from it].
"Existence arises from the mind alone"—this has been taught by those who speak the truth.
By what means were weapons abandoned by the mind? Who was he who tamed others and was free from fear?
Having made the world free from poverty through the perfection of generosity and the rest.
How was this world, filled with poverty, previously protected by him?
In the case of all people, there is the complete renunciation of one's entire possession along with its fruit, arising from the thought of relinquishment. (2) Akhila.
The perfection of generosity has been proclaimed; therefore, it is indeed that very mind.
Where shall those who are not bowed down by wealth find their end?
Faith and the mental state of abstention are considered the perfection of ethical discipline (śīlapāramitā).
How many wicked people, who are like the sky [in number], shall I slay?
When the mind of anger is slain, all enemies are slain.
To cover the entire earth, where will there be enough leather?
The earth becomes covered merely by the leather of one's sandals.
Indeed, the nature of speech cannot be prevented by me from arising.
I shall restrain my own mind; what is the use of restraining other things?
For one who desires companionship but acts with a sluggish disposition, that fruit [of companionship] does not arise.
That which belongs to the mind of even one person, such as its identity with Brahman and so forth.
All recitations and austerities, even those performed over a long period of time.
The All-Knowing One has said that one who acts with a different mind is merely acting in vain.
To destroy suffering and attain supreme bliss, they wander in vain through the sky.
Because of this, all these beings have not cultivated the secret of the mind, which is the universal Dharma.
Therefore, with my own mind, I have well protected this body.
Those who have made the protection of the mind their primary vow are truly my true ascetics through their many observances.
And just as those who are supremely impartial protect a forest with care;
Thus, those who dwell amidst the wealth of wicked people should always protect their minds with mindfulness.
Fearing even a mere fraction of the pain of a wound, I protect that wound with great care.
What is the use of wounding those with evil intent by means of the crushing mountains of Saṃghāta?
By dwelling in this dwelling, even a wicked person [is transformed].
A renunciant who dwells in the midst of women, even if lacking self-control, is not broken.
May my desire for gain, honor, and even this body and life be extinguished.
And no one else is more skilled than he at knowing the mother's mind at any time.
I join my palms in reverence to those who guard the mind from sensual desires.
And one should protect both mindfulness and clear comprehension with every jewel.
He is incapable of forest life, being distressed by hunters; likewise, with a distracted mind, he cannot protect himself in all his activities.

The Blessed One said: "Then, while seated cross-legged, one should [bind] these samaya-mudrās with the mind focused on fire—namely, desire, hatred, and delusion. These are the mind-vajra-holders and so forth."
Regarding the binding of the mind toward all deities, it is said: "With palms joined in reverence, one stands firm upon the stone among the hosts of all deities."

The Samaya-mudrā mantra: Oṃ namaḥ susiddhe sādhanī agre karuṇavaradaḥ taye (2) ativale namo 'stu varasiddhidāyakebhyo mahākṛtyaḥ svāhā. By these, the samaya of all mudrā-mantras is revealed. Thereafter...
As before, forming the vajra-mudrā, recollect the heart-mantra of Acala.
Mantra: Oṃ, homage to all the Vajras! Subdue the fickle ones, O fierce achievers! Hūṃ Phaṭ!

Then, while forming the Vajroṣṇīṣa mudrā, one should place the *śilāśī* [seal] upon the right fist and make the thumb white. Mantra: Oṃ namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvānām | Triśikhāgne namo 'stu te | Samantāguṇasamantāguruṇāvarāgradharmma |
Shaking off the net of afflictions and the suffering of the world, bestow [peace] upon that fierce one; therein, perform this threefold commitment, svāhā!

By reciting this, one does not fall away from the Mahāyāna, and its accomplishment becomes free from obstacles. Furthermore, by placing this great protection upon the five locations, one becomes powerful.
Having formed the *uttāna-añjali* (upturned palms) with the little fingers interlaced and the middle fingers outside, [recite]:
*suvi ihā mayāmahe hūṃ phaṭ*. Then, one should perform the armor-rite (*kavaca*) with the Great Armor Mudrā of the Invincible Vajra.
The two thumbs of the maidens are Śaṅkarā; by Time, the other [fingers] are [Śaṅkarī]. The roots are Śaṃsara-kṣamūla, and the middle fruits are for the sake of Ajivaja.
Mantra: Oṃ namo samantavajrāṇām | Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ vajramayara kavacaho vajra hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ, to all the Tathāgatas, hūṃ hūṃ svāhā. Oṃ, homage to all the Samantavajras!
O Uṣṇīṣa of all the Tathāgatas, Śītāntapatra! Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ! Protect me in this temple; grant peace and well-being, svāhā!

Then, one becomes even more worthy of worship by the gods and the Sālāyins. Having thus performed the protection of oneself, one should perform the protection of the place. There, with the Vajrāsana-mudrā, one should consecrate the seat as a vajra.

With the left hand placed palm-upward in the center of the vajra-paryaṅka posture and the right hand resting upon it, one assumes the Vajrāsana mudrā. The mantra is: Oṃ samantavajrānīḥ nama oṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ. Then, with the Vajrāśraya mudrā established in its own place, one should abide in the Vajrasamaya.

The *pañcamudrā* consists of the two ring fingers (*anāmikā*) and the two index fingers (*tarjanī*) joined together with their backs bent and turned inward; likewise, the two middle fingers (*madhyamā*) are joined, as are the two little fingers (*kaniṣṭhikā*) and the two thumbs (*aṅguṣṭha*). [Mantra: *praṇāmāñjali-ratānāmikā-yugaraṃ viparīta-pṛṣṭha-bhagnam iti | anāmikā-tarjanyau rūpa-rūpa-cakre tāveva deya-ati | evam etad viparīta-pṛṣṭha-gargga-madhyamā-suci tathā kara-kaniṣṭhikā-aṅguṣṭhau pañca-mudrā || mantra ||*
Oṃ, homage to all Vajras! Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ vajrāgrabhūvaṇe muḥ hūṃ phaṭ.
Then, one should place the vajra-flame outside that mudrā.
He performed the ritual for the one who grants fearlessness, having properly prepared the snake-charm, and he circumambulated it with devotion.
Vajra-flame. The mantra.
Oṃ, homage to all Vajras! Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ vajrajvāle hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!

Then, from the *sīmābandhanī* [rite]: having raised the index finger (*tarjanī*) and made a fist with the right hand, one should rotate it clockwise. This is the mantra for the *asīmāna-sīmābandhanī*: Oṃ namaḥ samanta-vajrāṇām | Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ mahāsīmābandha vajre vajriṇī hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Then, having performed the protective rites and remaining in one's own place,
while reciting "Buddha Bodhisattva," one should offer the *argha* with the *Tathāgatasambhava* mudrā.
Then the Siddhas, the givers of boons, pay heed to him.
For those established in the mudrās that grant liberation, the little finger is one's own Tathāgata; this is the mantra for the Śubhra-mudrā.
Oṃ, homage to those whose end is vajra! Oṃ, homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas!
To you who possess stainless, victorious splendor, who are free from passion, svāhā!

Then, when external perfumes are available for the ritual service, one should purify them with the Acalavajra mudrā and perform the eightfold worship with the respective mantras for the perfumes and other offerings.
Therein is the mantra for incense.
Homage to all the Tathāgatas who are the supreme fragrance of the unconditioned! O you who are stable like space, of great prosperity, accomplish all aims! Svāhā!
Therein is the Flower Mantra: *Namaḥ traiyadhvikānāṃ sarvatathāgatānām; mahāpuṣpe puṣpavati svāhā*.
The mantra for that lamp.
Homage to all the Tathāgatas who transcend the three times: *ayante jvalante dīpajyotisi khe svāhā*.
The mantra for the offering of meat and other substances.
Homage to all the Tathāgatas who are supreme in the subduing of the *namaḥ-steya* [sorcery]; *arara pavali devali dadāhiṃ mahābali svāhā*.
Then, he caused the manifold offerings present in the world-systems of the ten directions to shine forth.
With flowers, water-offerings, incense, lamps, and even unconditioned offerings, one performs the offering of the ten directions and the world-systems,
manifesting a vast array of splendors such as jewel-mountains, *kalpavṛkṣa* trees, and so forth, as well as oceans of water and jewels.
And those [objects] such as golden lotuses, and whatever others there may be—divine or human—within all the world-systems.
One should utter: "May all forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles—those [qualities] such as taste and so forth—issue forth for the sake of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas."
But one should thus carry out these very same offerings consisting of the mind.
Having formed the *pūrṇamudrā* with the fingertips slightly contracted and the palms joined in salutation (*añjali*), one should speak as follows:
By the supreme empowerment of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; by my own excellent vow, merit, and vidyā-mantra.

And with power, one should think: "In the circles of assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, there is a vast and sublime, inexhaustible great offering consisting of the practice of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, which is intensely devoted."
One should recite this Mahātrī Vidyārājñī, the empowerment of worship, eight times.
Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas! In every way, [to you who are] like a mass of clouds of vast majesty on all sides, svāhā!
Then, there arose oceans of clouds of melodic hymns praising the diverse qualities of all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
oceans of clouds of Dharma-hymns that pervade all world-systems and proceed everywhere.
Having reflected.
This collection of praises is equal to the ultimate nature; it is the emergence from the clouds of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
He recited the eight verses of the Queen of Spells, Kārttīvidyārājñī.
This is the Aparājitā [mantra] named Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣaśītāntapattrā.
The Great Pratyamgira, the Queen of Great Vidyas.
Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas! O you who possess the sword of the superknowledges that pierces everywhere, homage be to you, svāhā!
Then, as far as the world-protectors throughout all the world-systems.
In all oceans, they are equal to the non-existence of all sentient beings.
Having emanated clouds of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas from all objects of focus, [he]...

Having contemplated thus: "May all the sufferings of all sentient beings be pacified; may they attain the purity of the body and so forth of Samantabhadra, as far as the supramundane states exist in all world-systems," [one should recite].
This is the Aparājitā [mantra] named Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣa-śītāntapattrā.
One should recite the Mahāpratyāṅgirā-vidyā eight times over the king.
Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas! Homage to you, O Great Vajra, who brings benefit to all sentient beings! Abide, having empowered all phenomena for the sake of all! Svāhā!
And it is well known that all such acts as worship and the like are accomplished through the power of mantras and so forth.

And this is unwholesome for one who thus dedicates [it] toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, in the manner that the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, do not authorize. Whatever root of merit I have here—
And by this [thought], "In that way I dedicate," I have fully awakened to enlightenment through the merits of the conduct of Samantabhadra.
Oṃ! Vajrasattva, maintain the samaya; you are established by Vajrasattva.
Be firm for me; be well-pleased with me; be easy to nourish for me; be devoted to me.
Grant me all accomplishments! O you whose mind is action in all rites! Bestow glory, HŪṂ HA HA HA HA!
HO, Blessed One, All Tathāgatas! O Vajra-holder, release the vajra within me! Great Bhava!
Samayasattva ĀḤ.
Or the Pañcarakṣā [mudrā]: the two hands are joined back-to-back; the thumbs and little fingers are placed facing upward; the index fingers and ring fingers are bent toward the palms;
and the middle fingers and third fingers are fully extended.
Holding the thumb and middle finger together in close proximity.
As for the Satākṣara-mudrā, having formed the *saṃpuṭa-añjali* (the hollowed-palms gesture), one should press the two index fingers against the thumbs.
The ritual procedure for Śyemā is likewise well-expounded. Mantra: Oṃ namo sarvabuddhabodhisattvānām | Āḥ vīravajraśṛṅkhale hūṃ phaṭ ||
Then, one should bind the Samantāvabhāsoṣṇīṣa Dharmacakra mudrā, which is the synthesis of all mudrās.
With both hands well-restrained, having covered the middle of the nose with the nails.

With the tips of the thumbs and little fingers joined, one should place [the hands] in the form of a needle; likewise, the middle fingers are joined at their tips. This is the Uṣṇīṣa mudrā, which shines all around like a well-dug pit.
Having moved them together with the index fingers, one should begin by pressing nail against nail.
The Dharma-cakra mudrā is in the form of a circle. The mantras for these two are, respectively: ĀḤ SAHAṂ.
Oṃ, O wielder of the thunderbolt, shake them, cut them with the wheel, hūṃ phaṭ!

This is the Aparājitā, named Śītāntapattrā, the Great Pratyamgirā, the Queen of Great Vidyās belonging to all the Tathāgatas. Whichever of these two [mantras] is recited as a lethal incantation— whether standing or sitting, whether with the voice broken by weeping or other such states— the accomplishments (siddhis) will manifest before one.

Then, for the sake of swift accomplishment, one should bind the *dharmodayā* mudrā upon the head and recollect its mantra: with the left hand, form a fist and extend the index finger; likewise, extend the little finger and the thumb upward. The mantra is: *namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvānām āsarvatrāseke svāhā*.
Having recited the mantra of one's own mudrā once, one should display the samaya.
One's own mudrā, however, should be practiced according to the yoga.
Then, [there follows] the prostration to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
When the mind is being made to arise from its object, it proceeds according to how it has been directed by mantra.
Naked, she stands in the pratyālīḍha posture, emitting fierce rays of light.
She has two arms, her breasts are full and elevated, and she is red in color.
The fierce and powerful three-eyed one swiftly moved about with great agility.
Free from improper intentions, one should recite the syllables of the mantra with a single-pointed mind, and should not give way to weariness.
Then he recited the *Gaṇḍavyūha* and other sūtras that uplift the noble ones, as well as the *Sarvatathāgatahṛdaya-sakad-anatyavācana*, which resides in eighteen world-systems.
Having worshipped [the deity] who possesses infinite power and the fourfold life-force, one should say: "Homage to you, O Tujjātārāṇī!
Homage to you, O Nāhārasambhavārāṇī! Homage to you, O Nāhāramastavārāṇī! Having thus consecrated it with mantras...
This ball of alms-food is offered to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; it should be eaten in a moderate amount, it should be eaten in a moderate amount.
In this regard, the mantra is as follows: *Namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvānām | Oṃ vaṃ laṃ dade tejomālini svāhā*.

For one who has finished eating, according to the proper conduct, one should offer the remaining food by reciting the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* mantra multiple times and casting it as a *piṇḍa*. Thereupon, the awakened one bestows the attainment of happiness.
Having performed the confession of sins and other rites while resting after the meal, one should then remain within the garden of the True Dharma.
If one is capable,
even when away from home, one should perform all protections for the mantra and so forth.
Having performed the worship and other rites, one should proceed as before with the vajra.
The fivefold auspicious ornaments, such as the arched gateway and the enclosure wall, and so forth.
Another [form] should form a breastplate consisting of a garland of rays of light.
With their fingers interlaced and their brows furrowed in a frown.
Having formed a constant fist with the middle fingers...
In the form of a needle, extend the index finger; place it upon the third joint of that same [finger].
The two thumbs on the opposite side [of the palms] constitute the Māriṇī mudrās and mantras.

From the first watch of the night until the last watch, one should spend the day in the private recitation of the True Dharma.

With the middle [offering], he should bring forth the Perfectly Awakened One and the Bodhisattvas to his own bed, which is free from a couch; having prostrated, he should lead them forward and make this request:
May all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas empower me; may they grant the boon of supreme accomplishment, and may they pacify all calamities.
May this great vidyā, the Aparājitā Mahāpratyamgirā named Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣaśītāntapattrā,
which has been well-spoken, provide protection, concealment, rescue,
guardianship, and nourishment; may it grant peace and well-being, as well as the avoidance of punishment and the avoidance of weapons.
The neutralizing of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth.
May they provide protection; may they live; may they see a hundred autumns and a hundred years.
Thus, by this very procedure of Mahāpratyāṅgirā, may Mahāpratyāṅgirā, the Great Sovereign Queen,
who has been well-spoken, provide protection,
concealment, rescue, guardianship, preservation, peace, and auspiciousness.
The warding off of the staff; the warding off of weapons; the neutralizing of poison; the expulsion of evil spirits.
May they perform the binding of the boundary, the binding of the earth, and the protection for me,
my retinue, and all sentient beings, svāhā!
By this very ritual, the recitation of this *Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣa-śītāntapattrā-mahāvajraśṛṅkhalā-mahāpratyamgirā* should be performed daily until the full moon for the sake of protection;
or until the signs of success appear to one who has undertaken it.

Then, on lunar days such as the full moon, having observed a fast (*bhakta*), [the practitioners] should sit upon a seat made of wood chips, barley-straw, *yava* stalks, *khadira* wood, *saṃbalī* grass, or young shoots; or they may sit upon a pedestal of *kuśa* grass. In front of a shrine (*caitya*), a *bhaṭṭa*, a manuscript, or an image, they should perform the protection rite (*rakṣā*) by sprinkling a circular mandala with water.

The requisites for worship and so forth: Then, having formed the mudrās of the Buddhas and Dharmas of the past, one should recollect my mantra. Then, having formed the mudrās of one’s own deity, one should recite the mantra eight times and display the *samaya*. Then, having prostrated to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, one should take up the wheel, vajra, and other implements.

This praise of Vajraśṛṅkhalā, the Great Pratyamgirā, the King of the Three Samayas, was spoken in the Kalpa and sung by Vajradhara Vajrapāṇi.

Remover of the fear of enemies and poison; provider of enjoyments and other comforts within the kingdom; surrounded by one's own circle of followers; bestowing liberation through the offerings of devotees; establishing dharma that dispels misfortune; the sole path for attaining mokṣa;

You who effect the protection of people at every step, you who fulfill all desires, you whose mudrās are borne by Bhṛgu, you who remove the fear of enemies and ill-repute, and you who bestow sovereignty, enjoyments, and more.

For those who have abandoned their own [self-centered] paths and whose groups are sustained by the gift of knowledge, for those who have cleared the path of wealth and abide in the gift of knowledge— listen to the specific offerings for Bodhisattvas who do not turn back: having accumulated hundreds of thousands of virtues over ten million eons, and having made offerings to hundreds of thousands of infinite Buddhas.
For the benefit of the entire world, there arises a mind of Dharma belonging to those who have reached the further shore of patience through their vows toward others,
who follow the conduct of Hariśikha, and who have emerged from merit and wisdom.

The thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*) arises, equal to the Ten-Powered One, for those whose minds are vast and directed toward the vehicle of merit and wisdom; it remains engaged until the Buddhas of the three times have been honored,
purifying all realms through a dedication as expansive as the path of the sky.
By means of the meanings that have correctly come down and been transmitted, [one understands] all phenomena in their full extent.
For those who are constantly exerted for the sake of liberation and the welfare of the world, who delight in the qualities of the Victors,

and whose intention is set upon the conduct of awakening— the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*) arises as an activity for the benefit of the three worlds. This occurs when one possesses a perfectly focused mind through concentration on the knowledge of the Dharma, and when the wise are filled with great joy.
To those who delight in the dharma of giving, who are ever intent upon the welfare of the entire world.

To those who have gone for refuge to the Jina, who are committed to the vow of protecting sentient beings, who follow after wholesome qualities, who partake of the essence of patience, who recognize the excellence of virtues, and who have abandoned the festivals of pride;

Those who shatter the pride of the wicked, who are praised by the gods, and who are solely intent on protecting all beings.

O you who have struck down all obstacles, the sole honor of all the worlds; you who have established the ten powers as the grain [of your harvest], the most excellent among the five goddesses; the refuge for those in difficult straits—homage to you at all times!

"Two cubits in length," and so forth; "as you see," and so forth. Here too, it is indeed two cubits, minus twenty...
Regarding the twenty qualities, he states that the trident is white and consists of bliss, beginning with the words "half a cubit" and so forth.

"Two-fifths," and so forth; "five-fifths"; "of the sixteenth"; "of the first nourishment"; "in this case, the conjunction [is determined] by the western nourishment and the southern back"; "one should perform the *śāntika* rite in the forenoon, but the *pauṣṭika* rite in the afternoon."
Cruel rites are performed at midday, while rites for subjugation are performed at midnight. Weapons with unbroken points and those possessing two blades are auspicious.

These should be offered smeared with oil; likewise, at the *avoṭana* rite, the feathers of a tree-dwelling crow (*vṛkṣakākapakṣa*) are to be offered.

Through the power of the great meditations and the invocation of samādhi, for the sake of the supreme one who possesses the splendor of a manifested hood,
for the activity of the gods, for all sentient beings, and for the sake of Dharma, I am of the nature of Varuṇa.
All phenomena are pure by nature;
I am pure by nature. Hūṃ. I am of the nature of the deity who is pure by nature.
All phenomena are pure in body; I am the purity of the nature of the body, HŪṂ.
I am the very self of the deity whose nature is the purity of the body.
The speech of all phenomena is pure; the nature of speech is pure—HŪṂ.
I am the essence of the deity whose nature is the purity of speech. All phenomena are the purity of mind;

I am the purity of the nature of mind, HŪṂ. I am the essence of the deity whose nature is the purity of the nature of mind. All phenomena are the purity of the mantra; I am the purity of the nature of the mantra, HŪṂ. The nature of the mantra...

I am the essence of the pure deity. All phenomena are pure in their nature; I am pure in the state of the *tantra*. I am the essence of the deity, pure in the state of the *tantra*. All phenomena are pure in their mantra-nature; I am pure in the state of the mantra. Hūṃ.
I am the essence of the deity, pure through the state of mantra; all phenomena are pure through the state of yoga;
I am pure through the state of yoga.
I am the very self of the deity whose nature is purified through yoga.

In the right hand, by means of the syllable *A*, is the solar disc (*sūryamaṇḍala*). In the left hand, by means of the syllable *Ā*, is the lunar disc (*candramaṇḍala*). *Oṃ vajrapadmahasto hūṃ īṃ | oṃ vrūṃ āṃ jīṃ khaṃ hūṃ | oṃ rāṃ māṃ pāṃ trāṃ aṃ aḥ | oṃ nāgāṣṭaka rakṣa me jīvaṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā | oṃ phaṃḥ śīla* ||

The eradicator of all sins; the eradicator of all obstacles caused by sin; [the eradicator] of all calamities such as the four Māras and so forth; [the eradicator] of all humans and others, including the hosts of Asuras. Having thus meditated upon the pacification of all these calamities, today—

One who is sharpened by detachment, sharpened by seclusion, and matured through renunciation, cultivates the state of loving-kindness toward all directions. One who is sharpened by seclusion, sharpened by detachment, and matured through renunciation, cultivates the state of compassion.
The state of sympathetic joy is white with seclusion, white with dispassion, and matured through relinquishment;
thus it is called "the cultivation of the state of sympathetic joy."
The state of equanimity is purified by seclusion, purified by dispassion, and matured by relinquishment;
thus one dwells in the state of the nature of equanimity.
Having become equal toward all sentient beings, [one should visualize] one's own heart as the transformation of the white syllable *vaṃ*, which is the seed-syllable.

Abiding in the world-systems of the ten directions, including the gates, gods, humans, and nāgas; dwelling among all the hosts of deities, and even beyond them—summon! Oṃ Āḥ!
