This is the penetration of the four noble truths, the mind regarding all phenomena,
and the four foundations of mindfulness, until the complete attainment of all the qualities of a Buddha in this immovable world-realm.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candraketudhvajaśrī.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Candraśrī.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Prabhāśrī; oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Buddhakośamatiśrī.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Dharmakāyasamatishri.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Saṃghakosamatiśrī.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Mañjuśrī, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Nārāyaṇaśrī, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Kusumaśrī. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmajyotiśrī.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmajyotivikrīḍitābhijña.

Thus, hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Tathāgatas, headed by these, have assembled; they are inclined toward seclusion, inclined toward dispassion, and matured in renunciation, giving rise to unsurpassed mindfulness. 4.
Furthermore, O Vajradhara Vajrapāṇi, this is the Mahāvajroṣṇīṣa Mahāpratyamgirā.

The Great Queen of Vidya-mantras: perfectly pure, completely cleansed, the embodiment of omniscient wisdom, the secret of body, speech, and mind of all Tathagatas, the realization of the enlightenment of all Buddhas and Perfectly Enlightened Ones, [the essence] of all Tathagatas.
The unsurpassed realm of Dharma; the happy destination for those who have gone well; the complete defeat of all Māras by the Victors.
The state of being empowered by the ten powers; the totality of all those who possess the ten powers.
Omniscience is the source of all the knowledge of the omniscient ones; it is the source of all phenomena.
The perfect attainment of all Buddhas; the stainless, perfectly purified accumulation of merit and wisdom; the source of all great Bodhisattvas; and the excellence of all Śrāvakas.
The refuge of the Pratyekabuddhas; the sovereignty over all gods and humans; the foundation of the Mahāyāna; the source of the bodhisattva conduct; and the culmination of the noble path.
The non-interruption of the arising of the path of deliverance for those liberated through refinement.
The manifestation of the lineage of the Tathāgata, the great Bodhisattva, and the subduing of the family and clan.

The destruction of all adversaries; the defeat of all non-Buddhist sectarians; the subduing of the four Māras; the gathering together of all beings; the ripening of the noble path for those who follow all vehicles.
Concentration belongs to those who dwell in the four divine abidings; effort belongs to those whose minds are focused on a single object.
O you who have become the secret of body, speech, and mind; O conqueror of the four Māras; O noble one who releases the excellent [teachings].
The gathering of all sentient beings; the ripening through the Noble Path.
For those who travel by all means of deliverance, there is concentration for those who dwell in the four modes of abiding.
The pervasive [wind] consists of single moments of mind for those engaged in yoga through body, speech, and mind, and for those who are free from fetters.
It is the abandonment of all primary and secondary afflictions; it is the complete pacification; it is the liberation of all those who possess the ten powers;
it is the release from all bonds; it is the peace of all calamities; it is the source of all mental fluctuations; it is the non-decline of all prosperity; and it is the destruction of all misfortune.
The non-functioning of all doors to the lower realms, of the city of conceptual proliferation, and of the wheel of saṃsāra.
The turning of the wheel of Dharma; the raising of the parasol, banner, and flag; and the empowerment of the Tathāgata’s teaching.
In the teaching of all dharmas, there is swift accomplishment; for the bodhisattvas who practice the conduct of the mantra-entrance, there is the attainment through meditative cultivation.
For those bodhisattvas devoted to the perfection of wisdom, emptiness is awakening; it is non-dual.
For those devoted to the cultivation of penetration, there will be the accumulation of all the perfections.
Purification; the fulfillment of the perfections of all stages; penetration.
He penetrated the four noble truths correctly and realized that all phenomena are of one mind.
Of the four foundations of mindfulness, up until their complete fulfillment; this is [the essence] of all the qualities of the Buddhas, in the world of the indivisible Dharma.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnavyūhaketurāja!
Oṃ,
homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Raśmiśrīmerugarbha, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha whose name and glory are well-proclaimed.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnacandraketudhvaja.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vicitraśrī.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Suvikrāntaśrī.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Vicitraśrī.
With these as their leaders, hundreds of thousands of millions of Tathāgatas assembled together.
Settled in seclusion, settled in dispassion, and matured in relinquishment.
He cultivates the direction of unsurpassed mindfulness. || 5 ||
Furthermore, O Vajradhara Vajrapāṇi, this is the Vajroṣṇīṣa Mahāpratyamgirā.
O Great Queen of Spells! Completely pure, thoroughly cleansed, the wisdom of the omniscient one!
The secret of body, speech, and mind of all the Tathāgatas; the awakening of the Buddhas.
The realization of the perfectly awakened ones; the unsurpassed [realization] of all Tathāgatas.
The element of Dharma for those who have gone to a happy rebirth; the complete defeat of all Māras by the Victors.
The power of the ten powers; the state of being all-possessing among all those who possess the ten powers; the knowledge of the omniscient one.
The awakening of the Buddhas of all the Tathāgatas, who have purified body, speech, and mind.
The realization of all the perfectly awakened ones; [the realization] of all the Tathāgatas.
The unsurpassed realm of phenomena.
The state of those who have transcended all states of existence; the complete defeat of all Māras by the Victors; the possession of the power of the ten strengths.
The arrival of all those possessing the ten powers; the source of the wisdom of the omniscient ones;
the complete attainment of all Buddhas; the stainless and perfectly pure state of all Buddhas.
The fulfillment of the accumulations of merit and wisdom; the source of birth for all great bodhisattvas.
The power of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; the sovereignty over the excellence of all gods and humans.

It is the foundation of the Mahāyāna; the source of the bodhisattva’s conduct; the culmination of the noble path of right application; the touchstone of those who are liberated; and the birthplace of the path of deliverance.
The non-interruption of the Tathāgata’s power; the increase of the lineage and family of the great Bodhisattvas.
The suppression of all opposing disputants; the destruction of all non-Buddhist sectarians; the defeat [of them].
O Noble One, conqueror of the four excellent hosts of Māra! Compendium for the ripening of all sentient beings in the noble path!
For those who travel by every means of deliverance, and for those who dwell in the four divine abidings, there is meditative concentration.
Pervasive effort belongs to those with a single-pointed mind; it belongs to those engaged in body, speech, and mind.
The abandonment of all fetters; the complete pacification of all primary and secondary afflictions.
Liberation from all obscurations; release from all bonds; pacification of all calamities; a mine of all mental excellencies; and the non-decline of all prosperity.

The destruction of all calamities; the [closing] of all doors to [unwholesome] means; the non-occurrence of the city of conceptual proliferation regarding the true meaning; the turning back of the wheel of saṃsāra; the setting in motion of the wheel of Dharma; the raising aloft of the parasol, banner, and flag of the Tathāgata’s teaching; and its empowerment.
In the teaching of all dharmas, there is swift accomplishment.
The practice of the mantra-gate; the attainment through cultivation by the bodhisattvas who engage in that practice.
For those bodhisattvas devoted to the perfection of wisdom, emptiness is awakening; it is non-dual.
The cultivation of penetration will belong to those who are engaged in the accumulation of all the perfections.
Complete purification; the fulfillment of all stages and perfections; and penetration.
The penetration of the four noble truths and all phenomena with a single mind.
Of the four foundations of mindfulness, up to their complete fulfillment; this is the [perfection] of all the qualities of a Buddha.
In the world of those who have attained supreme victory.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Sugandhapadmaratnaśrī.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Vikrāntagāminī.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Samantāvabhāsaśrī.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnapadmasupratiṣṭhitaśrīreṇdrarāja.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Pratibhānaśrī.

With these as their leaders, hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Tathāgatas have assembled; they cause the unsurpassed mindfulness—which is inclined toward seclusion, inclined toward dispassion, and matured through relinquishment—to pervade the directions. 6.
Furthermore, O Vajradhara, O Vajrapāṇi, this is the Mahāvajroṣṇīṣa,
the Mahāpratyaṅgirā, the Great Queen of Spells, which is perfectly pure, completely cleansed, and the wisdom of omniscience.
They have become the secrets of body, speech, and mind.
The awakening of all Tathāgatas, the perfect and complete enlightenment of all Tathāgatas,
by name, is the commitment of all Tathāgatas.
The unsurpassed realm of phenomena, for those who have attained a happy rebirth, the supreme vanquisher of all Māras.
The power of the ten powers; [the state] of all those who possess the ten powers; omniscience, [the state] of all those who possess the knowledge of the omniscient.
The arrival; the full attainment; the full attainment of all dharmas; the stainless, perfectly pure merit of all Buddhas; and the fulfillment of the equipment of wisdom.
The source of birth for all great bodhisattvas; the field for all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; the excellence of all gods and humans; and the foundation of the Mahāyāna.
The culmination of the conduct of a Bodhisattva; the perfection of the noble path of right application.
The non-interruption of the path of deliverance for those liberated through insight.
Of the lineage of the Tathāgata.
The manifestation; the subduing of the great bodhisattvas; the destruction of all supreme adversaries; the defeat of all non-Buddhist heretics; the crushing of the fourfold army of Māra.

The gathering of all sentient beings; the ripening of the Noble Path; for all those traveling the way of definitive emergence; the meditative concentration of those dwelling in the four Brahmavihāras; the pervasiveness of those with one-pointed minds;
the yoga of those endowed with body, speech, and mind; and the abandonment of those who are unattached to sense objects.

The complete subsiding of all primary and secondary afflictions; liberation from all obscurations; release from all bonds; peace for all misfortunes; a mine for all mental agitations—a mine for all mental agitations; and [the end] of all prosperity’s decline and all calamities.

The piercing of the spokes; the closing of all doors to the means [of rebirth]; the truth in the city of liberation; the non-functioning of the wheel of saṃsāra; the setting in motion of the wheel of Dharma;
the raising aloft of the parasol, banner, and flag of the Tathāgata’s teaching; and the empowerment thereof.

In the teaching of all dharmas; swift accomplishment; the practice of the mantra-entrance; for the Bodhisattvas who engage in conduct; the attainment through meditative cultivation; for those devoted to the perfection of wisdom.

For Bodhisattvas who are devoted to the cultivation of penetration, there will arise the realization of emptiness as non-duality; this is the complete purification of the equipment of all the perfections, which constitutes the perfection of all the stages.
The fulfillment of fulfillment; penetration; of the four noble truths correctly; the oneness of all phenomena.
The penetration of the mind, from the establishment of the four foundations of mindfulness until their complete fulfillment.
This is the ocean of all the qualities of the Buddhas; it is the abode of the clouds of Dharma.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Sūryottamaśrītejornibhāśaya.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, the Glorious King of Splendor, the Immeasurable Destroyer.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Guṇaratnaśrīyatejonibhāsa.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Dharmapratiśrī.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Prabhāvyūhasukīrṇabuddhi.
With these as their leaders, hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Tathāgatas assembled.
Whitened by seclusion, whitened by dispassion, and transformed by relinquishment.
He cultivates the direction of unsurpassed mindfulness. 7.
Furthermore, O Vajradhara Vajrapāṇi, this is the Mahāvajroṣṇīṣa,
the Mahāpratyaṅgirā, the Great Queen of Spells, perfectly pure, completely cleansed, and the wisdom of omniscience.
The secret of body, speech, and mind of all the Tathāgatas; the awakening of the Buddhas.
The realization of the perfectly awakened ones; the unsurpassed realm of phenomena of all Tathāgatas; the destination of those who have gone well; the complete defeat of all Māras by the Victors.
The power of the ten powers; [the lineage] of all those who possess the ten powers; of all those who possess omniscient knowledge; the scripture.
The realization of all Buddhas, stainless, perfectly pure merit.
The fulfillment of the equipment of wisdom; the source of all great bodhisattvas; the birthplace of all śrāvakas.
Of the Pratyekabuddhas.
The field of all gods and humans, the perfection of excellence, the foundation of the Mahāyāna.

The culmination of the conduct of a Bodhisattva; the perfection of the noble path; the touchstone for those who are liberated; the non-interruption of the lineage of the Tathāgatas, which is the path of emergence and arising.
The increase of the Great Bodhisattva; the suppression of all proponents of other doctrines; the destruction of all heretics; the defeat of the four Māras by means of the Noble Net.
For the ripening of all sentient beings in the Noble Path, for all those who proceed by way of definitive deliverance.
Concentration belongs to those who dwell in the four divine abodes; meditative absorption belongs to those with one-pointed minds;
yoga belongs to those endowed with body, speech, and mind; and abandonment belongs to those who have severed the fetters. All [these] are included therein.
The subsiding of the afflictions and secondary afflictions; the liberation from all obscurations.
Liberation from all bonds.
The pacification of all anxieties; the subduer of all mental agitations.
The loss of all prosperity; the destruction of all calamities; the non-functioning of the gates of all means [leading to] the city of the True Goal; and the setting in motion of the wheel of saṃsāra.
The raised parasol, banner, and flag of the Wheel of Dharma; [the raised parasol, banner, and flag] of the Tathāgata’s teaching.
The empowerment for the teaching of all dharmas; swift accomplishment; the practice of the mantra-vehicle.
The realization through cultivation of the bodhisattvas who practice [the stages].

For those Bodhisattvas who are devoted to the perfection of wisdom, there will be the realization of emptiness; for those devoted to the cultivation of penetration into non-duality, there will be the accumulation of all the perfections.
Purification: the perfection of all stages. Purification: the fulfillment of the perfections of all stages. Penetration: of the four noble truths correctly.
He penetrated all phenomena with a single mind regarding the four foundations of mindfulness.
Until its completion: this [is the collection] of all the qualities of the Buddhas, in the world named Abhimukhi.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnajotisahasrakiraṇaikakapilamuni.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Sahasrajotiśrī.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śubhakanakaśrī.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, the Glory of the Array of the Resounding of the Sky.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened Buddha, the Glory of the True Nature of All Phenomena.

With these as their leaders, hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Tathāgatas have assembled; they cultivate the unsurpassed mindfulness that is inclined toward seclusion, inclined toward dispassion, and matured through relinquishment. 8.
Furthermore, O Vajradhara Vajrapāṇi, this is the Mahāvajroṣṇīṣa, the Great Pratyaṅgirā.
The Queen of Great Knowledge; perfectly pure; completely cleansed; the wisdom of the Omniscient One.
The secrets of body, speech, and mind of all the Tathāgatas; the awakening of the Buddhas.
The realization of all perfectly awakened ones; the unsurpassed [realization] of all Tathāgatas.
To those who have gone to the state of the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), to the Sugatas; to the Victors who have achieved the defeat of all Māras.
The power of the ten powers; [the lineage] of all those who possess the ten powers; of all those who possess omniscient knowledge; the scripture.
The realization of all Buddhas; the stainlessness of all Buddhas.
Supremely pure; the fulfillment of the accumulations of merit and wisdom of all the great bodhisattvas.

It is the source of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; it is the sovereignty over the excellence of all gods and humans; it is the foundation of the Mahāyāna; it is the origin of the bodhisattva conduct; it is the culmination of the noble path; it is the touchstone for those seeking liberation; and it is the birthplace of the path of deliverance.
The non-interruption of the lineage of the Tathāgatas; its increase; and the subduing of the great bodhisattvas.
The destruction of all rival disputants; the defeat of all non-Buddhist heretics.
O Noble One, you who have slain the four hosts of Māra with the hawk-like [wisdom], you who bring to maturity the path of the noble ones!
For those who travel by way of all deliverances, there is the fourfold Brahmā-vihāra; for those who dwell in the dwelling of meditative concentration.

Meditation is the conquest of the four Māras by those who possess a single-pointed mind and whose body, speech, and mind have become secret. It is superior to the noble army; it is the gathering of all sentient beings and the ripening of the noble path.

For those traveling by every vehicle of deliverance, there is concentration; for those dwelling in the four divine abodes, there is meditative absorption; for those with unified minds, there is yoga; for those engaged in body, speech, and mind, there is the severing of fetters; for all afflictions and secondary afflictions, there is abandonment; for all those possessing the ten powers, there is tranquility; and for them, there is liberation.
The liberation from all bonds; the pacification of all acquisitions; the source of all mental fluctuations; the loss of all prosperity; and the destruction of all misfortune.
The cessation of all gateways of means, the destruction of the city of conceptualization, and the non-functioning of the wheel of saṃsāra.
The setting in motion of the Wheel of Dharma; the raising of the parasol, the banner, and the flag.
Of the teaching of the Tathāgata.
The empowerment for the teaching of all dharmas; swift accomplishment.
The practice of the mantra-entrance; the attainment through cultivation by the Bodhisattvas who engage in such conduct.
For those bodhisattvas devoted to the perfection of wisdom, there will be the realization of emptiness,
non-duality, and the cultivation of penetration; there will be the purification of the equipment for all perfections, and the penetration that brings to fulfillment the perfections of all the stages.
The penetration of the four noble truths and the single-minded realization of all phenomena as one.
This is the [summary] of all the qualities of a Buddha, from the foundations of mindfulness up to their complete fulfillment.
In the world of the immortals.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Mahāhā Amoghasiddhi.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Mahāmṛtābhā Amoghapāśa.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnasaṃbhava, the Great Ocean of Jewels.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Great Akṣobhya, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Mañjuśrī, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened Buddha.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Vipaśyin, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened Buddha.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Sikhin, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Viśvabhū, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Krakucchanda, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One.

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Kanakamuni. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Kāśyapa. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat Śākyamuni.
To the perfectly enlightened ones.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Great Vairocana, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One.
With these as their leaders, hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Tathāgatas had assembled.
One cultivates the foundation of mindfulness that is inclined toward seclusion, inclined toward dispassion, ripened in relinquishment, and unsurpassed.
Furthermore, O Vajradhara, O Vajrapāṇi!
This is the Mahāvajroṣṇīṣa, the Great Pratyamgirā, the Queen of Great Vidyās.
Perfectly pure, completely cleansed, consisting of the omniscient wisdom, and having become the secrets of body, speech, and mind.
The awakening of all Tathāgatas; the perfect awakening of the Samyaksambuddhas; their realization.

Of all the Tathāgatas; of the unsurpassed Dharmadhātu; of those who have gone well to their destination; of the conquerors who effect the defeat of the power of all Māras; of the possession of the ten powers; of all those endowed with the ten powers.
The source of the wisdom of the omniscient ones; the complete attainment of all Buddhas.
The stainless, perfectly pure accumulation of merit and wisdom of all the Buddhas has been fully perfected.
The source of all great bodhisattvas, of all sentient beings, and of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
The Kṣatrapa Sarvadeva, the rival of all men, the foundation of the Mahāyāna.
The culmination of the noble one’s practice of the bodhisattva path is perfect.
The polishing of the Noble Path; the liberation of those who are liberated; the non-interruption of the arising of the path of deliverance;
the lineage of the Tathāgatas; and the flourishing of the great Bodhisattvas.
The destruction of all those who hold opposing views; the defeat of all non-Buddhist sectarians.
The power over the four Māras; the noble subduer of armies; the noble gatherer of all sentient beings.
The ripener of the path for all who travel by way of liberation; the fourfold concentration of the Brahmās.
For those who dwell in the monasteries, meditation for those with one-pointed minds, and yoga for those disciplined in body and mind.
The abandonment of all [afflictions] extending for twenty yojanas; the complete pacification of all primary and secondary afflictions.
Liberation from all obscurations; release from all bonds; [freedom] from all afflictions.
Peace for all mental fluctuations; a makara for the loss of all prosperity.
The destroyer of all misfortunes; the truth that closes the doors to all states of woe.
The non-functioning of the city of solitude; the turning of the wheel of cyclic existence; and the turning of the wheel of Dharma.
The parasol, banner, and flags have been raised; this is the empowerment of the Tathāgata’s teaching.

The swift accomplishment of the teaching of all dharmas; the practice through the gateway of mantra; the attainment of meditative cultivation for those bodhisattvas who practice; and [the realization] of those devoted to the perfection of wisdom.
For Bodhisattvas, it is the awakening to emptiness, non-duality, and the cultivation of penetration.
For those who are diligent, there will be the complete purification of the equipment for all the perfections.
The fulfillment and penetration of all the stages and perfections.
He has thoroughly penetrated the four noble truths with a single-minded focus on all phenomena.
Of the four foundations of mindfulness, until their complete conclusion: all Buddhas.
This is the [work] of Guṇānīya, in the world of those named Sādhumati.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vajrapramardin, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened Buddha.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Suvarṇaratnārcis.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnākarachatrukuṭa.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Nāgeśvararāja.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Vīrasenaśubhakīrttikiraṇa, the Sage Kapila.
Thus, led by these [leaders], hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Tathāgatas assembled.
He cultivates that which is brightened by seclusion, brightened by dispassion, matured by relinquishment, and directed toward unsurpassed mindfulness.
Furthermore: O Vajradhara, O Vajrapāṇi! This is the Great Vajroṣṇīṣa, the Great Pratyamgirā, the Queen of Great Mantras, perfectly pure, completely cleansed, and the wisdom of omniscience.
The secret of body, speech, and mind of all the Tathāgatas; the awakening of the Buddhas.
The realization of the perfectly awakened ones; the unsurpassed realm of phenomena of all Tathāgatas; the destination of those who have gone well; the complete defeat of all Māras by the Victors.
The state of being endowed with the power of the ten powers; the arrival of all those who possess the ten powers and the wisdom of omniscience.
The perfect attainment;
the perfect attainment of all phenomena; the stainless, perfectly pure merit of all Buddhas; the fulfillment of the equipment of wisdom; the source of all great Bodhisattvas.
The power of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; the sovereignty over the excellence of all gods and humans.

It is the foundation of the Mahāyāna; the source of the bodhisattva’s conduct; the culmination of the noble path; the touchstone of liberation; the origin of the path of deliverance; the non-interruption of the lineage of the Tathāgatas; the manifestation of the great bodhisattva; and the subduing [of adversaries].
The destruction of all opposing disputants; the defeat of all non-Buddhist teachers.
And the supreme among the four Māras; the Noble One releases [them] through gathering; [for the sake] of all sentient beings.
The ripening of the noble path for all those who proceed toward liberation; the meditative concentration of the four brahmavihāras.
For those who dwell in various abodes, meditation is for those whose minds are unified.
Yoga is the abandonment [of defilements] by those who are endowed with body, speech, and mind, and who are disjoined from them.
The subsiding of all afflictions and secondary afflictions; the liberation from all obscurations.
Liberation from all bonds; pacification of all calamities; prevention of all mental agitation; protection against the loss of all prosperity; and the destruction of all misfortune.
Of all the gates to the lower realms; by means of truth; of the city of destruction; the non-functioning of the wheel of saṃsāra.
The turning of the Wheel of Dharma; the raising of the parasol, the banner, and the flag.
The empowerment of the Tathāgata’s teaching; the swift accomplishment of the instruction of all dharmas.
The practice of the mantra-entrance; the attainment through cultivation by the practicing Bodhisattvas.
For those bodhisattvas devoted to the perfection of wisdom, non-duality is realized when emptiness is not rejected.
It pierces through for those devoted to meditative cultivation; it penetrates all the perfections.
The purification of the accumulations; the perfection of all stages; the fulfillment; and penetration.
The penetration of all phenomena as a single mind through the four noble truths.
Of the four foundations of mindfulness, up until their complete fulfillment; this is the measure of all the qualities of a Buddha.
Among the immovable [beings], there is no world.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Viranandin, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnavyūhaśrī.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amoghadarśin, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened Buddha.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnacandraprabhāsaraśmiśrī.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, the Glory of the Wisdom-Treasury of the Buddhas.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, the glorious Dharmakośamati.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Saṃghakośamati-raśmi-śrī.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed Ones, the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Ones: Satyakauśalamati, Śrīrasmiśrī, and the rest.
Thus, led by these [Bodhisattvas], hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Tathāgatas assembled.
He cultivates the mind directed toward seclusion, directed toward dispassion, ripened by relinquishment, and unsurpassed mindfulness.

The Blessed One said: "Furthermore, noble son, to the east of this buddha-field, there are as many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of worlds as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges."
Having transcended the Buddha-fields, [he reached] the world-system Padmāmalā.
Adorned with various jewels of diverse virtues; having various jeweled peaks, storehouses, and so forth.
In the vicinity of trees and lotus ponds, where there is a single species, immeasurable Bodhisattvas have awakened.
In that world-system, they hear the Dharma in the presence of the Tathāgata Pratibhānavyūha.
The great tree named Indrīṇāma consists of jewels; its value is hundreds of thousands of millions.
There is a lotus made of precious jewels. Therein dwells the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Aparimitaguṇapratibhānavyūha; [his name] is not unsurpassed.
He has fully awakened to perfect enlightenment.
There, the bodhisattvas are seated upon lotus thrones; they behold his miraculous powers.
Those bodhisattvas who have come from all the world-systems [honored him] with various flowers and various incenses.
Having performed worship with various umbrellas, various banners, various flags, and various lamps and so forth.
She is stationed there.
Furthermore, son of good family, to the south, beyond as many as ten million,
a hundred thousand nayutas, or as many as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, buddha-fields.
The world-system named Padmānām is adorned with various jewels of excellent qualities.
[It was] filled with various jewels, heaps of charcoal, and so forth; adorned with trees and lotus ponds; where [beings] who have only one more birth [remain].

The Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, the Tathāgata Guṇavyūha, hear the Dharma there in that world-system from his presence; the jewel-trees there consist of various kinds of jewels, and at their base are ten million.
Possessing hundreds of thousands of millions of colors, with lotuses made of precious gems for its arrows; there, on that first night—
In the presence of the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha Guṇaratnavyūharāja, [I take refuge] in the Unsurpassed [Enlightenment].
He has perfectly awakened to complete enlightenment; there, the bodhisattvas are seated upon lotus thrones.
He beholds his miraculous displays. Those bodhisattvas who have come from all the world-systems honor him with various flowers, various incenses, various parasols, various banners, and various flags.
Having worshipped with various lamps and so forth, and remaining there, furthermore, O son of good family:
In the western direction, there are millions, hundreds of thousands, or billions of Buddha-fields.
Having passed beyond Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, there is a world-system named Padmā, adorned with various jewels of virtue.
Adorned with various jewel-pinnacles, charcoal-heaps, and so forth, as well as trees, lotus ponds, and groves; where there is a single species [of being].
The Buddhas and Bodhisattvas hear the Dharma from the presence of the Tathāgata Guṇavyūha.

In that world-system, there is a jewel-tree composed of various jewels. At its root, there is a hundred thousand million *niyutas* of petals made of jewels in the form of lotuses. There, during the first watch of the night, in the array of the jewels of qualities—
Not toward an Arhat, nor toward a perfectly awakened one; not toward unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

He has attained perfect enlightenment. There, upon the lotus throne, are the bodhisattvas. Behold his miraculous displays! Those bodhisattvas have come from all the world-systems, [offering] him various flowers.
With various incenses, various parasols, various banners, and various flags.
Having worshipped with various lamps and so forth, she remained there.

Furthermore, noble son, to the north of this buddha-field, beyond hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, there is a world-system named Padma.
Adorned with various jewels of diverse qualities, featuring various jeweled peaks, hearths, and the like, as well as trees and lotus ponds.
Adorned [by them], where bodhisattvas of a single birth have awakened in the presence of the Tathāgata Padmottama.
To the Tathāgata, Arhat, Aparimitaprabhāsavyūhaśukīrṇabuddha.

The Perfectly Enlightened Ones hear [this] in that world-system. In that world-system, there is a great bodhi-tree named Indra; it is composed of jewels. At its base, there are ten million nayutas of hundreds of thousands of golden leaves.
There is a lotus made of jewels; there, during the first watch of the night, no Arhat exists within the interior of the lotus.
In the Perfectly Awakened One; not in the Unsurpassed Perfect Awakening; in the Perfectly Awakened One.

Enlightenment was fully realized. There, seated upon lotus thrones, the bodhisattvas behold his miraculous displays. Those bodhisattvas who have come from all the world-systems [honor him] with various flowers, various incenses, various parasols, various banners, and various food offerings.
Having worshipped with various banners and various lamps, they remained there.
Furthermore, noble son, in the direction of the southeast, beyond hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of buddha-fields—
as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges— there is a buddha-field.

The world-system Padmā is adorned with various jewels of diverse qualities; it is beautified by various jeweled pavilions, trees, lotus ponds, and so forth, wherein there is but a single Buddha and Bodhisattvas.
The array of the Dharma; they hear the Dharma in the presence of the venerable Tathāgata.

In that first world-system, there is a great Bodhi tree named Indra. It consists of jewels; at its summit, there are a hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* golden leaves and lotuses made of jewels. There, during the first watch of the night, to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Śrī by name—Sahasraśvara, Meghagarjita, and Pratibhānavyūha—[he spoke].
In the Perfectly Enlightened One; not in the Unsurpassed [Vehicle]; in the Perfectly Enlightened One; not in the Unsurpassed [Vehicle].
He has perfectly awakened to supreme perfect enlightenment. There, the bodhisattvas are seated upon lotus thrones.
These are his miraculous displays: the bodhisattvas who have come from all the world-systems [honoring him] with various flowers, various incenses, various perfumes, and various parasols.
With various banners, various food offerings, various pennants, and various lamps.
Having performed worship, they remained there.
Furthermore, noble son, in the southwestern direction, beyond hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of buddha-fields— as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges— there is [a world].
The world-system Padmā is adorned with various jewels of virtue and possesses various forms of fine gold and gems.

With trees such as gabled pavilions, adorned with lotus ponds, where the Bodhisattva of One Birth, the Tathāgata Padmottama, resides; before him is an immeasurable array of light, strewn with Buddhas.
The Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas hear it there in that world-system.

There is a great Bodhi tree named Indra. At its base, there are millions, billions, and hundreds of thousands of silver and gold leaves, as well as lotuses made of jewels. There, during the first watch of the night—
By the Arhat Padmottara, the Truly and Completely Enlightened One; [there is] no higher truly and completely perfect enlightenment.

They have attained perfect awakening. There, seated upon lotus thrones, the bodhisattvas behold his miraculous displays. All those bodhisattvas who have come from all the world-systems [honor him] with various flowers.
With various incenses, various perfumes, various parasols, various banners, and various food offerings.
Having worshipped with various banners and various garlands of lamps, they remained there.
Furthermore, noble son, to the northwest of here, beyond hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, there is [a world-system].

The world-system named Padmā is adorned with various jewels of diverse virtues; it is graced with various jeweled gabled mansions and the like, and beautified by trees and lotus ponds. Therein, one who has awakened to a single birth resides.
The Bodhisattvas [stood] before the Tathāgata Padmottara, [and] Sahasreśvara and Meghagarjita.
They hear the name Prativyūhaśrī, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, in that world-system.

There is a great Bodhi tree named Indrā, made of jewels. At its base, there are hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of silver and gold leaves and jewel lotuses. There, during the first watch of the night, [he dwells] upon the supreme lotus.
Not by an Arhat; not by a Samyaksaṃbuddha; not by [the attainment of] unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

He has attained perfect enlightenment. There, upon a lotus throne, the Bodhisattvas are seated; they behold his miraculous powers. Those Bodhisattvas who have come from all the world-systems [honour] him with various flowers.
With various incenses, with various perfumes, and with various parasols.
With various banners, various food offerings, various flags, and various garlands of lamps.
Having performed worship, they remained there.
Furthermore, noble son, in the northeastern direction, beyond hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, there is [a land].
The world-system named Padmā is adorned with various jewels of diverse qualities, featuring various jeweled gabled palaces and other structures.
Adorned with trees and lotus ponds, there [dwelt] a Bodhisattva of the same lineage who had awakened in the presence of the Tathāgata Padmottama,
before the King of Splendid Radiance and Majestic Power named Sūryāttamavyūha.

To the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha; there, upon a lotus throne, the Bodhisattvas were seated. They beheld his miraculous powers (*prātihārya*). All those Bodhisattvas who had come from all the world-systems [honored him] with various flowers and various incenses.
With various perfumes, various parasols, various banners, various food offerings, and various flags.
Having worshipped with various garlands of lamps, they remained there.
Furthermore, noble son, in the south-western direction, beyond hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, there is [a world].

Abounding in the jewel-like virtues of lotuses, such as embers from a hearth and the like, and adorned with trees and ponds, there was a single species of lotus. There, bodhisattvas who had awakened [to their destiny] stood before the Tathāgata Padmottama for incalculable millions of kalpas.
They listen to the Buddha, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, who has arisen from the ocean.

In that world-system, there is a great Bodhi tree named Indra. It is composed of jewels and consists of precious gems. At its base, there are ten million, one hundred thousand nayutas of lotuses made of silver, gold, and jewels. There, during the first watch of the night, the Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmottara appeared.

He had not yet fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. There, seated upon the lotus throne, the bodhisattvas beheld his miraculous powers; those bodhisattvas who had come from all the world-systems honored him with various flowers, various incenses, various perfumes, and various parasols.
Having worshipped with various banners, various food offerings, various flags, and various garlands of lamps,
they remained there.
Furthermore, noble son, in the upward direction, beyond hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, there is [a world-system].
The world-system named Padmāna.
Adorned with various jewels of diverse virtues; [possessing] various jeweled peaks, hearths, and so forth.

Adorned with trees and lotus ponds, there the Bodhisattva, awakened to a single birth, stood before the Tathāgata Padmottama— [he] who was like pure gold, whose roar resounded through the sky, and who possessed the radiant splendor of majestic arrays.
The Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas hear [this] in that world-system.

There is a great bodhi tree named Indrā; it is composed of precious jewels. At its base, there are hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of lotuses made of silver, gold, leaves, and jewels. There, during the night—
To the Tathāgata, Arhat, Tejorāja, whose glory consists in the transformation of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā).

O Perfectly Enlightened One! Not by means of lotuses is one an Arhat; O Perfectly Enlightened One! It was not upon a lotus seat that unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment was realized there; rather, the Bodhisattvas were seated [upon them] and beheld his miraculous displays.
Those bodhisattvas who had come from all the world-systems [honored him] with various flowers and various incenses.
With various perfumes, various parasols, various banners, various food offerings, and various flags.
Having worshipped with various garlands of lamps, they remained there.

Then the Tathāgata Padmottara, having understood their dispositions and latent tendencies, for the benefit and welfare of beings, out of compassion for the world, and for the benefit of gods and humans, set in motion the irreversible wheel of Dharma for the sake of fulfilling the Mahāyāna. The Bodhisattva said:
"Blessed One, how long will that world-system remain, and for how long will the Tathāgata Padmottara abide with his True Dharma?"
The Blessed One said:
Noble son, such will be the lifespan of the Tathāgata Padmottara.

They shall remain for thirty intermediate kalpas teaching the True Dharma. In whatever place Bodhisattvas are born, their lifespan shall measure forty intermediate kalpas. Furthermore, O son of good family, formerly this world-system was named Candrottama, yet it was not so completely pure.

[It was] strewn with pure beings, just as this world-system is now. O son of good family, in the world-system Candranāyā, there was a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Candrotama. He taught the Dharma for twenty intermediate eons, throughout his entire life. Of him—
At the time of his final nirvana, sixty-one bodhisattvas, by virtue of their vows, departed for other buddha-fields;
as for those bodhisattvas who remained—
He said this, O Blessed One:
Tonight, at midnight, Candrottama Tathāgata will enter parinirvāṇa.
The True Dharma will remain for ten intermediate kalpas; what is the meditative absorption at the end of the True Dharma?

Immediately thereafter, they shall fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Furthermore, at that very time, there was a bodhisattva named Gaganasamudra, by virtue of his previous vows.
"You, O son of good family, have been prophesied by the Tathāgata Candrottama: 'You shall become [a Buddha]...'"
For one who has not yet entered parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma remains for ten intermediate kalpas. It shall endure through both the period of its presence and its subsequent disappearance.
He will pass away during the first watch of that very night, specifically in its final portion.

They shall fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. He shall become a Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha named Padmojjvala. Therefore, one should perform [this] for the sake of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva. By means of which...
The Tathāgata Candrottama was approached by a thief who came there in all various forms; having performed worship to the Bodhisattva Candrottama, he addressed the Blessed One as follows.
We wish to hear from the Blessed One about the intermediate kalpas following the instruction of the Blessed One.
To bend the mind toward restraint with careful attention.
There, indeed, Vajradhara Vajrapāṇi addressed the bodhisattva Gaganasamudra, the noble son Candrottama, and said to him: "Take this up, noble son."

This [is] the *Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣaśītāntapattrā-nāmāparājitā-mahāpratyamgirā-mahāvidyārājñī*, the entrance into the gateway of the *dhāraṇī* that brings about omniscience, [as taught by] all the *samyaksaṃbuddhas* of the past and the future.
This *Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣavyavalokitā-nāma-samādhi* has been taught for the sake of the bodhisattvas consecrated as crown princes,
and for those who are currently in all the world-systems throughout the ten directions.

The Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, teach while remaining present; they will also teach those who will become Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the future time. They will teach the Bodhisattvas who have been consecrated to the position of crown prince.
It is as follows:
Oṃ jali jali mahājali | Niphatke made mahāsande | Devāṃ aṭi caṭi ṭake ḷ ḷ ra ḷ kte ||
Amimakasi! Sili sihiḷi cili cili tili ruruke! Mahāruruke! Victory to the Invincible One! Victory to Jayamati!
In peace, she is the one whose resonance is peace; she is without root and completely severed.
In the terrifying of Māra’s army; in the liberated, the utterly pure; in the fearless, the deliverer from fear.
The Vidyā that ends with the sound *hāradohora*, O most excellent of Vidyās, [is used] for the subjugation of those who surround one.
Favor for those who speak according to the Dharma; protection for those who speak according to the Dharma.
This is the word of illumination, the word of liberation from me, concerning the four foundations of mindfulness.
The saffron robe of the Buddha; free from "mine" and "not mine"; in the meaning that is non-dual, in the meaning that leads to the beyond;
for the sake of liberation from the world, apply yourself to its cultivation. This is the word of illumination regarding the stage of resolute confidence in the four kinds of finality.
To the speaker; to the bearer, who maintains; to the one of secret and auspicious radiance; to that fruit, the supreme fruit, the fruitless;
to the one without "I," O such-and-such, O liberated, O fully released; to the one who has caused liberation; to the one without worldly attachment; to the unattached.
Thus: he drinks; the one swift in pleasure; the swiftest; the serpent-like; speaking thus; not having gone, not having gone.

In the entire world, O you who have become manifold, O you who are the source of the stream of nectar, O giver, O intoxicated one, O you who possess the splendor of a dwelling, O you who are fruitless yet bear the fruit of liberation.
This is the word of illumination, the stage of resolute belief for those three who have not yet been observed.

This is the *Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣa-śītāntapattrā*, named the *Aparājitā Mahāpratyamgirā*, the great and heroic vidyā-mantra. It is to be recited without omission. This is its fruit: the fruit of the path of determination (*niyāma*). O you who have gathered and adorned [it], for whom this mantra is [effective]: it is unerring, not even slightly erring; it is the mantra that cuts away and removes [all obstacles].
Abiding in the body of the Ten Powers; well-established in the arrow; possessing sharp intelligence; illumination; exceedingly sharp; possessing supreme intelligence.
Present; in the previous strike; of the four; of the Perfectly Awakened Ones' abandonments.
Eat, O you who are the state of liberation! This is the state of illumination.

This is the Great Queen of Spells, the Unconquerable Mahāpratyamgirā named Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣaśītāntapattrā: *anemanyamane mamani vire viratosame samitāvi śānte muktani rakṣame same samasame kṣaye akṣaye ajiti śānte saniṣṭo dhāraṇī*.
He spoke thus: "O you who possess light! O you who have set out upon the jewel! O you who possess flavor! O you who possess the essence! O you who possess the Maruts!"
In the demonstration of destruction; in the demonstration of the lamp of the world; in the four analytical knowledges; in the stage of resolute belief.
This is the word for illumination.
This is the Aparājitā named Śītāntapattrā, the Uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas.
Mahāpratyamgirā; Mahāvidyārājñī; O you who shine with protection; O you who manifest!
And the manifestation of the light of knowledge.
In the radiance; having transcended the earth with the left sense-faculty; all, all, me.
O destroyer of all sins! O you whose face is like a cow’s hoof-print! O you who bring about the disappearance of the worlds!
Of the four bases of psychic power, this is the state of liberation; this is the state of illumination.
This is the Aparājitā named Śītāntapattrā, the Uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas.
Mahāpratyamgirā | Mahāvidyārājñī | Acala | Acale | Buddhe Buddhapracale |
In the being, the accomplishment of the house; in the trembling, the prohibition is joined; in the supreme palace; having given Soma to the Moon; immovable in the immovable;

in the non-falling, the non-wavering, the non-falling; moving forward, spreading; in the leader, the extreme state; in the desire, the powerful one; in the marketplace, the innate and fierce wheel; in the eye; of the senses and the powers; through me, the state of liberation.
This is the term "illumination."
This is the Aparājitā Mahāpratyamgirā named Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣaśītāntapattrā.

O Great Queen of Spells! You who abide in the wheel of existence! O Holder of the Wheel! O Diamond-Wheel! O Most Excellent Bestower of Boons! O Upholder of Modesty! O You who are invoked with praise! O Hūhūre! Just as [you are] the destroyer of pride; just as you are beyond the reach of enemies; just as you are the destroyer of fear! O Extractor of Truth! O Extractor of Old Age and Sickness! O Extractor of Prowess! O Cure!

The accomplishment of the path; the accomplishment of meditative concentration; the accomplishment of wisdom; the accomplishment of liberation; the accomplishment of the knowledge and vision of liberation; the accomplishment of the stars; the accomplishment of the planets; the accomplishment of the moon.
The accomplishment of the sun; the fourfold increase of the verses; by the Tathāgata; marvelous; perfectly praised.
The perfectly awakened one; the non-awakened one; the awakened one here; the awakened one there; in Nihaṃgamadyara.
Worthy of the Arhats; white there, O Māṅgharaṇi, you who have reached the city of Puṇḍarīka, you whose movement has ceased, you who are tranquil, you who are stainless.
Not bound by the non-existent. Chiṃchinī, Chiṃchindramaṇi. He who is in the midst of the outer and inner. Hanare.
Bhara, bhara; bhinde; bhire, bhira. Rūpare! Śaraṇe! Dāraṇe! Pravartta! Pravartte!
In the lineage of Varaṇa: Vidambumāvarapumā, Brahmacāriṇī, Indravatī, Indracarī.
Dhīdhīrāyaṇī, Maheśvaralalanī, Mamusumā, Aramiṇī, Ekākṣaririvañcanī.
Carasti ābhicandārasuraḥ | Sarvasuraḥ | Ābharasuraḥ | Punakanitā ||
Maṇḍitāmāyinī, Karṇijabhāmā, Gandharvā, Aḍarunimakarā, Bhirohinī.
In the Siddhamata; in the Virokamata; empowered by the Buddha; at the gateway of the dhāraṇī; this is the word of illumination for the state of liberation through the ten powers.
Immediately thereafter, when the Blessed One had introduced this *Sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukha* [Door to the Dhāraṇī of the Aspects of Omniscience],
this great trichiliocosm world-system shook in six ways and was likewise illuminated throughout all the world-systems in the ten directions.
Born from the stainless samaya, they appear clearly; those who abide within them possess meditative concentration and dhāraṇī.
The bodhisattvas attained patience through the power of the Tathāgata, each in their own respective [realms].
They vanished from the buddha-fields.
This is the Aparājitā named Śītāntapattrā, the Uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas.
Mahāpratyaṅgirā | Mahāvidyārājñī | Hṛdayadhāraṇī | Dhāraye | Dvācaye |
He illuminates it perfectly; he becomes one who speaks with ease regarding the Blessed One.
Having paid respect, I receive the Sūtras and Śāstras; by merely reciting them once, [the merit is attained].
Even with a perfectly focused mind for ten million eons.
Oṃ, homage to the Three Jewels! Oṃ, homage to the Buddha! Oṃ, homage to the Dharma! Oṃ, homage to the Saṅgha! Oṃ, homage to Mañjuśrī! Oṃ, homage to all Buddhas!

Oṃ Mahāpratyāṅgirā Uṣṇīṣa Cakravartin! Bind, bind all yantras, tantras, mantras, bonds, trees, and deities! Whatever fear or the like may arise here for those who dwell here, [bind it] by whatever means!
Chinda 2 bhinda 2 hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā.
Oṃ ciri ciri giri giri miri miri hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā.
Oṃ, the paralyzer, the immobilizer, the deluder, hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Oṃ vajra-uṣṇīṣa mahā-pratyaṅgira hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā.
Oṃ vajraśṛṅkhalāre hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā.
Oṃ vajraśṛṅkhāre ātmarakṣā hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā.
Oṃ padmo uṣṇīṣa vimale hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
Oṃ, O Śītāntapatra, oṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā!
Oṃ vajra-uṣṇīṣa-śītāntapatre oṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā.

Having taken the name of the person to be accomplished, one should hold it in the direction of the void.
Having performed the dismissal of them with *hūṃ*, one should accomplish all activities.
And that which is carried away by the wind, such as "nira" and so forth, from the *samādā* and *arūṇa* [stages].
Having pierced the left [channel] and having inscribed it, this is the complete pacification in every respect.
On the third thorn, one should draw [the figure] on a thorn in a secluded spot in front.
Oṃ hrīṃḥ ṣṭrīṃḥ vikṛtānana hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
Bring happiness! Kill! Expel! Subjugate! Cause enmity! Bring peace!

The seed-syllables joined with the letter *kāra* (the nasal *m*) effect pacification (*śānti*), nourishment (*puṣṭi*), and subjugation (*vaśa*).

Then the Blessed One [addressed] Varuṇa and the other nāgas, together with their retinues.
Varuṇa the Nāga king, Mañjuśrī the Nāga king, and Maṇicūḍa the Nāga king.
The nāga king Maṇi; the nāga king Maṇikaṇṭha; the nāga king Māli; the nāga king Raktamāli; the nāga king Śīta; the nāga king Vatsa; the nāga king Bhadra; the nāga king Subhadra;
the nāga king Dundubhi; the nāga king Upadundubhi; the nāga king Āmratīrtha.

The Naga King Maṇisuta; the Naga King Dhṛtarāṣṭra; the Naga King Virūḍhaka; the Naga King Virūpākṣa; the Naga King Vaiśravaṇa; the Naga King Śakatamukha; the Naga King Cāṃpeyaka; the Naga King Campaka; and the Naga King Gautama.

From time to time they will send down rain; from time to time they will thunder; from time to time they will manifest a state of longing; and all diseases and calamities will be pacified.

All these nāga kings had previously gone forth; they had assembled and were seated there with eighty-four hundred thousand *koṭi-niyuta* groups of nāgas. Then, at that time...
All the nāga kings, together with their retinues, rose from their seats, arranged their upper robes over one shoulder,
placed their right knees upon the ground, and extending their joined palms toward the Blessed One, bowed down to him countless times.
With offerings of supreme and diverse delights— flowers, incense, lamps, perfumes, tastes, touches, garlands, ointments,
powders, robes, parasols, banners, vajras, bells, flags, silk streamers,
musical instruments, drums, cymbals, and songs; with jewel-flowers, jewel-lotuses, and pearl necklaces.
With the world filled with the scent of *nāgapuṣpa* flowers and pearls, it resounded with a deep rumbling as it was driven by great winds.
Uttering great roars and delightful sounds, sounding the cry of the Dharma, they covered the Blessed One with great reverence and in manifold ways, and circumambulated him.
Having performed circumambulations, they stood in a secluded place; standing in that secluded place, they made aspirational prayers.
In all the oceans of world-systems, [there are] the atoms of earth, water, fire, and wind.
[It is] equal to the manifestation of all forms, [consisting of] atoms as subtle as dust.
In each and every atom of the ultimate measure.
They have completely transcended all groups and oceans; they are incalculable, incomparable, inconceivable, and inexpressible.
Having transcended oceans of bodily assemblies, at one time, presiding over immeasurable and incalculable clouds of serpent-oceans, facing all directions, from every single atom and particle of dust,
they pervade all quarters with unbroken clouds of offerings.

With oceans of clouds, we shall pay homage to, revere, and worship all the oceans of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas— namely, those who are immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, incomparable, and beyond measure.
By means of oceans and clouds of the power of universal conduct, which are ineffable and indivisible,
they pervade the intermediate space of the sky; just as they do by means of oceans and clouds of the physical forms of Bodhisattvas,
so too [do they pervade it] with all the colors of jewels.
By means of oceans of clouds of mandalas of the bodies of all suns and moons, dense with rays of light.
With clouds of oceans of all-jewel-holding flowers; with clouds of oceans of gabled pavilions illuminating all jewels; with clouds of oceans of trees of all powders filling the sky.
With ocean-like clouds of all fragrant incenses and manifestations of all forms; with ocean-like clouds of flowers that bring forth all jewels;
and with ocean-like clouds of celestial palaces that illuminate all jewels.

With clouds of oceans of all kinds of powdered trees from the sky; with clouds of oceans of all kinds of fragrant incense and displays of all forms; with clouds of oceans of the sounding of all kinds of musical instruments and roars.
Having ascended into the sky, which was completely covered by clouds over the ocean and by all kinds of fragrant trees,
[he stood] amidst the clouds over the ocean.
With these as their leaders, there were immeasurable, incalculable, equal, measureless, noble, ineffable,
and indivisible clouds of all kinds of offerings, clouds of oceans, and clouds of [offerings].
We shall honor and revere the oceans of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
We honor and worship [the Buddhas] by means of oceans of clouds of king-jewels from the womb, illuminated by the sphere of all arrays. Having pervaded the entire expanse of space,
we shall revere, respect, honor, and venerate the oceans of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
We worship with oceans of clouds of jewel-kings, arrays of rain from all-pervading radiance.
With all jewels blazing forth, with the sound of the *niryyāmaṇi* and the ocean-clouds of the king of jewels.

With ocean-clouds of jewel-kings that resound with the voices of all the Buddhas, Dharmas, and Saṅghas, expanding in every direction; with ocean-clouds of the radiance of Buddha-emanations from rays of light facing in all directions.

With ocean-clouds of jewel-kings that manifest the miraculous displays of the Tathāgatas’ palaces within inconceivable Buddha-fields; with ocean-clouds of Vairocana-jewel-kings that reflect the bodies of Buddhas amidst clouds of various jewels and precious dust; having established themselves, they pervaded the expanse of space.
We shall honor, revere, and respect the oceans of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
We worship with oceans of clouds of various jewel-fragrance and flower-pavilions that are indivisible; with oceans of clouds of various food-offerings from all directions and pavilions.

With clouds of oceans of filaments from all kinds of flowers; with clouds of oceans of gabled pavilions adorned with necklaces of various jewels; and presiding over the intermediate space of the sky covered by clouds of oceans.

With ocean-like clouds [of palaces] pervading the ten directions; with ocean-like clouds of jewel-peak mansions whose interiors are filled with the array of light from the rays of the Tathāgata, equal in number to all sentient beings.
With ocean-like clouds of gabled palaces, which are arrays of canopies adorned with necklaces of all kinds of jewel-dust;
With ocean-clouds of gabled pavilions adorned with all manner of arrays, emitting rays of light in every direction;
and with ocean-clouds of flowered archways and networks of bells hanging from all sides.
Abiding in the midst of the vast expanse of the sky, we shall honor, revere, respect, and worship the oceans of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
With oceans of clouds of lion-thrones, filled with rains of jewels and adorned with exquisite necklaces of gold and various gems.
With ocean-like clouds of lion thrones whose interiors are variegated by the radiance of flowers.
With ocean-like clouds of lion thrones with variegated centers of sapphire, gold, and lotuses;

with ocean-like clouds of lion thrones with variegated centers of lotuses adorned with jewels; with ocean-like clouds of lion thrones with centers of lotuses ablaze with all kinds of jewels; [and] the resonance of the form of the Buddha.
Having pervaded and overspread the entire expanse of space with oceans of clouds of lion-thrones whose interiors are filled with lotuses and rays of light,
we shall honor, revere, respect, and worship all the oceans of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

With ocean-clouds of trees of various jewels of all fragrances; with ocean-clouds of fragrance-emitting trees whose leaves and palms extend in every direction like clouds; with ocean-clouds of trees whose infinite light issues forth from all arrays; and with trees that manifest a single array in the form of all trees.
With oceans of clouds of all kinds of flowers, and with oceans of clouds of trees obtained from all clouds of flowers.

With oceans of clouds of trees that emit delightful sounds equal to the resonance of all musical instruments; with infinite tree deities whose radiance consists of the various and wonderful arrays of the circles of all bodhisattvas; and with oceans of clouds of trees that open up treasuries of all kinds of jewels and garments like the sun.

With oceans of clouds of lion thrones whose interior is filled with lotuses of jewels of infinite color; with oceans of clouds of lion thrones whose interior is illuminated by the king of all-jeweled faces on every side.
With ocean-like clouds of lion thrones in their interiors, adorned with arrays of every kind of ornament.
With clouds of oceans of lion-thrones from the interior of garlands of lamps emitting rays of various jewels.
With oceans of clouds of lion thrones whose interior is a city of jewels emitting universal sounds.
With oceans of clouds of lion thrones containing all perfumes, flowers, lotuses, necklaces, and jewels;
With ocean-clouds of lion thrones made of the essence of the king of jewels, which manifest the array of the seats of all Buddhas.
With oceans of clouds of jewel-treasury lion-thrones, adorned with jewel-essence clouds and decorated with beautiful, hanging necklaces of variegated jewels;
With ocean-clouds of lion-thrones, the splendor of whose crossbeams is adorned with all kinds of trees, jewels, and gems.

Having occupied the sky, which was completely covered by oceans of clouds of lion-thrones whose interiors were illuminated by the sun and adorned on all sides with networks of *kinkinī* bells made of various fragrant jewels,
[he] [honored] all the Buddhas.
From the ocean of bodhisattvas, we shall honor, revere, esteem, and worship them.

With clouds and oceans of canopies of all wish-fulfilling jewel-kings; with clouds and oceans of arrays of all flowers, whose filaments are made of sapphire gems and which are wish-fulfilling jewels; with clouds and oceans of canopies of all fragrant jewel-canopies; and with clouds and oceans of canopies of forms of lamps with jeweled flames.
With ocean-clouds of jewel-kings that manifest all Buddhas and resound with the light-orbs of their voices;
With oceans of clouds of canopies that manifest the radiance of all arrays of variegated jewels and garments.
With oceans of clouds of jewel canopies, radiant with the blazing light of all kinds of flowers and other offerings.
With ocean-like clouds of canopies of blazing flames that pervade all directions with the sounds of various bells.
With clouds of oceans of lotus-canopies made of mani-jewels and crystal, variegated with networks of lotuses of infinite color;

Having taken his place within the expanse of the sky, which was completely covered by oceans and clouds of banners and canopies illuminated by rays of beautiful golden hair, and by oceans and clouds of lion-thrones that manifested as inconceivable arrays of all possible arrangements.
With ocean-clouds of canopies of jewel-kings proclaiming the sound of the compassion of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
with ocean-clouds of canopies of garlands of light-rays from various jewels;
with ocean-clouds of variegated canopies adorned everywhere with networks of bells resounding and radiant with the light of dust-particles of universal jewels.

With clouds and oceans of canopies adorned with all kinds of jewel-trees and *śāla* trees; with clouds and oceans of canopies of the rays from the eyes of the gods, of the king of jewels, and of all fragrances, flowers, and incense; with clouds and oceans of canopies radiating everywhere the light of sandalwood powder; illuminated by the vast and variegated wisdom of the Buddhas.
With clouds of oceans of parasols that pervade the universal array, we shall honor, revere, respect, and worship the oceans of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas without distinction.

With ocean-clouds of mandalas of light from all jewels; with ocean-clouds of unadulterated mandalas of light from the rays and graspings of all jewels; with ocean-clouds of mandalas of light illuminated by clouds of all flowers; [and] with the emanations of Buddhas from the rays of all jewels.

By clouds of oceans of light-mandalas; by clouds of oceans of light-mandalas contained within the radiance of the parasols of all Buddhas; by clouds of oceans of light-mandalas that are jewel-umbrellas resounding with the Buddha-fields of universal gates; by the rays of the king of jewels from the lineage of all musical instruments and jewels.

By means of ocean-like clouds of circles of light that manifest the various marks of infinite forms for the sake of sentient beings; by means of ocean-like clouds of circles of light that emit delightful sounds arising from the vows of all Buddhas.

With clouds and oceans of all the circles of assemblies; with clouds and oceans of the light-orbs of the king of jewels whose sound disciplines all beings within the circles of all assemblies; we shall pay homage to the oceans of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
We shall revere, honor, and worship [them] with unbroken clouds of oceans of light-rays from all jewel-treasuries,
and with clouds of oceans of light-rays of all forms, sounds, fragrances, tastes, and tangibles.

With clouds of oceans of light-rays from all jewels; with clouds of oceans of light-rays radiating the thunderous roar of the mantras of all Buddhas; with clouds of oceans of light-rays illuminated by the array of parasols of all Buddhas.

With ocean-like clouds of rays from palaces of every flower; with ocean-like clouds of rays from the dust of every jewel; with ocean-like clouds of rays proclaiming the succession of all eons, the appearance of Buddhas, and the ripening of sentient beings; [he manifested] the inexhaustible jewel-treasury of sentient beings.
With clouds and oceans of rays from the filaments of all flowers.
With ocean-like clouds of light-rays that manifest the array of all seats.

With ocean-clouds of jewel-radiance having the color of unalloyed gold; with ocean-clouds of radiance from the king of jewels, the universal light; with ocean-clouds of radiance illuminating the array of vast parasols of all Buddhas.
With clouds of oceans of rays of all fragrances; with clouds of oceans of rays of all arrays.

With ocean-clouds of light-rays emanated by all Buddhas; with ocean-clouds of light-rays named "The Filaments of Various Jewel Trees"; with ocean-clouds of light-rays of all kinds of garments; with ocean-clouds of light-rays of the King of Manis named "The Resounding Sound of the Infinite Conduct of Bodhisattvas"; and with the light-rays of lamps made of all mani-jewels and pearls.
By means of oceans and clouds of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas that are undifferentiated, and by means of supreme clouds and oceans,
we shall honor, revere, respect, and worship them from the ocean.

With ocean-clouds of all kinds of fragrant flowers of diverse colors; with ocean-clouds of networks of lotuses with the radiance of all jewels; with ocean-clouds of circles of light from jewels and gems of infinite hues.
With oceans of clouds of banners and canopies, illuminated by rays from beautiful, auspicious forms and golden filaments;

With clouds of oceans of pearl-treasures of every kind of jewel; with clouds of oceans of powdered sandalwood and incense of every kind of jewel; with clouds of oceans of parasols of every kind of jewel; with clouds of oceans of inconceivable arrays, reflections, and ornaments of magnificent displays; and with a sweet, auspicious, and beautiful resonance.
With ocean-clouds of king-jewels; with ocean-clouds of necklaces of jewel-wheels illuminated by the sun.
With clouds of oceans of infinite treasuries of jewels; with clouds of oceans of all the bodies of Samantabhadra;
from the ocean of clouds of all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, we shall honor and revere them.
We would honor and worship.

Having thus made this aspiration for their forms, those nāga kings circumambulated the Blessed One three times, prostrated at his feet, and being permitted by the Blessed One, sat down upon their respective seats. They were as follows: Madājñānāvabhāsa, Śrītejolakṣmī, and so forth.

O you of firm valor, whose body is as solid as a diamond, supremely stainless; O banner of pure qualities, with the radiance of the sun, whose form is free from blemish; *bhara* (2), *saṃbhara* (2), *dundubhe*.
(2) O you of great radiance, who have dispelled the blinding darkness of great delusion and are fully perfected in the weapon of wisdom!
The aggregate of the mind of loving-kindness, the ocean of the Buddhas’ qualities,
the lotus of the factors of enlightenment, the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, and the eighteen unique attributes of a Buddha—
may this auspicious merit, endowed with pure dharmas, attain the profound splendor of the Buddha-dharma.

O you who have attained vast excellence, O Blue One! O eldest and most excellent in all worlds, O supreme among the powerful, O unsurpassed and unattached one! Dha-ra dha-ri dhu-ru śāntamate! Ca-ra ci-ri cu-ru pa-ra pi-ri pu-ru pa-ra! By the approval of the Buddhas, O Great Pratyamgira, svāhā!

It may be as follows: *Oṃ sara siri suru nāgānāṃ | java jivi juvu mahānāgā āgacchata buddhasatyeneha jambudvīpe pravarṣadhvaṃ | vara viri vuru dharmasatyeneha | sarvanāgānāṃ vāhanayiṣyāmi maitrīcittena.*

By the truth of the empowerment of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, may [this] come to rest upon the Mahāyāna, O Sovereign of Great Nāgas! By the power of the Buddhas, of all dharmas, and of the qualities of the great Bodhisattvas: bha-ra (2) bhi-ri (2) bhū-ru (2) mahā-jalāmbu-megha-vāhinī.
The retinue went to Mahābhujangadvīpa with a mind of loving-kindness.
O you who delight in the colors, foods, and scriptures; O Ghaṭa (2), Ghiṭi (2), Ghutu (2); O you of fierce embrace and great speed!
O you with flickering tongues and great venom, having conceived thoughts of loving-kindness, rain down [your blessings].
In this Jambudvīpa, by the truth of all Tathāgatas, svāhā!
Taṭa (2) ṭiṭi (2) ṭuṭu (2) Mahāmani! Wearing a crown and crest, she appeared in the form of a venomous serpent.
She dances; by the truth of Vajradhara, the empowerment of jewels in Jambudvīpa, svāhā!
Kiri kiri, kara kara, kuru kuru, O you who dwell in the great waters, you who advance with a great frown!
Come with minds of loving-kindness and release showers of rain here in Jambudvīpa.
By the empowerment of the essence of all Tathāgatas, Vajrapāṇi issues this command.
Rala (2), rili (2), rulu (2); may all the bhūta-serpents become accomplished in the *vikata* [form].
By the truth of all Tathāgatas: ghama ghimi ghumu svāhā.

O great nāgas of unimpeded strength and prowess, you who uphold fiery splendor, let a rain of showers fall here upon Jambudvīpa! Svāhā! Oṃ sara siri suru svāhā! Ho there, O great nāgas!
Remembering his own family and lineage, he releases showers of rain. By the empowerment of the truth of all the gods here in Jambudvīpa, may Māra be driven away! Svāhā!
By the empowerment of the truth of Brahmā, may it rain here in Jambudvīpa; svāhā!
By the truth of Śakra, let the great nāgas pour down rain here in Jambudvīpa, svāhā!
By the truth of the four noble truths, may there be a rain here in Jambudvīpa; svāhā!
By the eighth truth, may the great nāgas rain down here in Jambudvīpa; svāhā!
To the great nāgas Varṣaṇa and Mahānāga, by the truth of the stream-enterer here in Jambudvīpa, svāhā!
O great nāgas who rain down [blessings], there is no falsehood here in Jambudvīpa; svāhā!
O great nāgas who rain down [blessings], by the truth of the Pratyekabuddhas, may there be well-being here in Jambudvīpa! Svāhā!
By the truth of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, may the great nāgas rain down here in Jambudvīpa; svāhā!

By the truth of the great nāgas who cause rain, through the empowerment of the truth of all Tathāgatas, may there be *svāhā* here in Jambudvīpa! By the truth and the vow of all the gods, may all calamities cease here in Jambudvīpa; *svāhā*! By the truth of all the nāgas, may it rain here upon the great earth in Jambudvīpa! *Svāhā*!
Svāhā! By the truth of all yakṣas, may they protect all sentient beings; svāhā!
By the truth of all nāgas, may it rain down here; by the truth of the Dharma, svāhā!
By the truth of all the Gandharvas, take away all calamities of human beings; svāhā!
By the truth of all the Asuras, may all malevolent constellations be dispelled; svāhā!
By the truth of all garuḍas, may they show loving-kindness toward all nāgas; if they should release great torrents of rain here in Jambudvīpa, svāhā!
By the truth of all kinnaras, may they bring peace to evil and gladden all sentient beings.
Svāhā! By the truth of all the great nāgas, release the spread-out torrents of rain; restrain them!

*Pañcavarṣāvaraṇāni svāhā.* By the truth of all human beings, protect all human beings; *svāhā*. *Kara kara kiri kiri kuru kuru svāhā.* *Dara dara diri diri duru duru svāhā.* *Nata nata niti niti nutu nutu svāhā.* *Oṃ Śuśīghravāhinī Mahāmeghāmbu svāhā.*

O Cloud-bearer! O Cloud, Lord of the Great Clouds, Svāhā! O You who have opened the torrent of great clouds, O Creator of the origin of clouds, O Cloud, O Timely Cloud, O Roaring Cloud, O Dweller in the Cloud, O Lord of the Great Clouds, O Wearer of Cloud-Garlands, O Adorned by Clouds, O One whose Vehicle is the Cloud!
Dwelling in the clouds, roaring like thunderclouds, born of the clouds, surrounded by clouds; she who resides in vast clouds,
who wears the clouds as a sacred thread, and who brings forth the harvest— homage to her, the Blessed One, the Mother of the Nagas!
O Great Cloud! In the realm of the illustrious Jyotirvasa, where there is the touch of coolness and the whirlwinds of great winds.

In the sport of the Great Naga, may the Blessed Great Goddess rain down this dhāraṇī through the accomplishment of the sixteen [syllables] by the truth of the Buddha here in Jambudvīpa, svāhā! Ghara ghari ghuru ghuriṇi ghuma ghumanavarṣamahāmeghamāriṇī vidyutkarāyamāriṇī!
She who supports all serpents, she who wears garments of great cloud-silk, she whose range of activity is the foremost of all poisons,

she who carries forth the array of great clouds, she who leads with the sound of royal music— O Goddess Mahāmeghamāriṇī, who impels the sky of the Blessed Ones, who wields the terrifying radiance of lightning-flames, [homage] to all the Tathāgatas!
By truth, may all the nāgas cause rain to fall here in Jambudvīpa; svāhā!
Oṃ yara yari yuru svāhā || jala jili julu svāhā || gara giri guru svāhā ||

Therefore, life ends in death. For one who is born, there is no non-death. Thus it was said, O monks.

"Monks, there is no freedom from death for one who is born; even for kings, O monks, and for Kṣatriyas who have been consecrated with the head-anointing and have attained sovereignty and power over the provinces."

Having completely conquered the great circle of the earth, they dwell [therein]. For them, life indeed ends in death; life is bounded by death. There is no non-death for one who is born. The Pratyekabuddhas are like the rhinoceros horn; they bring bliss to themselves alone.
