life terminates in death. There is no such thing as non-death for one who is born. Thus spoke the Sugata, the Teacher of the world beyond, [saying]: "Impermanent indeed are conditioned phenomena; their nature is to arise and perish. Arise!
They cease; their suffering comes to an end, just as [the potter's wheel ceases] by the potter.
A vessel made of clay lasts only until it breaks; in the same way, the life of sentient beings ends with their final dissolution.

In each and every one of the countless, immeasurable world-systems that exist in their various dimensions.
In this world-system, there have been countless and immeasurable Buddha Bhagavāns who have entered final nirvāṇa.
Among them, the Aparājitā named Śītāntapattrā is the Mahāvidyārājñī Mahāpratyaṅgirā.

From the first production of the thought of awakening, based upon the teaching and discourse of the Dharma, until they have fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; until they have entered final nirvana in the realm of nirvana without remainder; and as long as the True Dharma does not disappear—in this entire interval.
Whatever root of merit there may be associated with the six perfections, and whatever [merit] those disciples possess—
Those who have set out in the vehicle hear of the basis of meritorious action consisting of giving, the basis of meritorious action consisting of ethical discipline,
and the basis of meritorious action consisting of cultivation; as well as the roots of goodness belonging to those in training and those beyond training.
And those which belong to those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.

The aggregate of ethical discipline, the aggregate of meditative concentration, the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation; and that which is the wish for the welfare [of others], and that which is immeasurable and incalculable great compassion—by those Blessed Buddhas.
He was a teacher of the Dharma; and having trained in that teaching of the Dharma, some attained the fruit of stream-entry, while others attained arhatship or the state of a pratyekabuddha.
The descent of the Bodhisattvas into my womb, their roots of merit,
and whatever roots of merit were planted by them toward those Tathāgatas while they were staying in the world or had passed into parinirvāṇa.
Having summarized all that, he rejoices in the rejoicing that is immeasurable and worthy of rejoicing.
By the eldest, the most excellent, the best, the preeminent, the most refined, and the supreme.
With the unsurpassed; with the ineffable; with the incomparable; with the peerless—[I] rejoice. Thus I rejoice;
that rejoicing is a basis of meritorious action associated with all sentient beings.
Having made it common [to all], one should dedicate it toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, thinking: "May this become a sustainer for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment."

Furthermore, a bodhisattva established in the vehicle speaks thus and dedicates his mind in such a way that, by means of those objects of focus, even that mind which has not yet arisen [is dedicated] toward unexcelled [enlightenment].
These things are not real entities; they are dependent designations according to how they are perceived, just as it was by those sons of good family.
They have been made into signs.
This is the Aparājitā [mantra] named Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣa-śītāntapattrā.

Mahāpratyamgirā, the Queen of Great Vidyās. She is bowed to by those who have bowed to reality and by others as well. Just as those belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle—noble sons who have taken her as their sign—have dedicated [their merits] toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment; furthermore, she is the Uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas.

Śītāntapatrā, Aparājitā by name, Mahāpratyaṅgirā, the Queen of Great Vidyās— if even these ten vidyās were not present, then the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, would have been rendered as mere signs by those who are separated from consciousness and lack the means of support.

Whatever roots of merit exist in those ten directions within the world-systems, based upon which [they have made vows] until the duration of the True Dharma— including those belonging to those who follow the vehicles of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas— [all these he dedicates].
The roots of the roots of wholesome merit of sons of noble family and daughters of noble family.
The roots of merit of those who have entered the stream, those who are once-returners, those who are non-returners, and those who are arhats—summarizing all of these together.

Having condensed [the merit] and dedicated it toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, one should not, through the application of signs, fall into the perversion of perception— just as perceiving the impermanent as permanent.
The perversion of perception, the perversion of mind, and the perversion of view [regarding] suffering as happiness.
Perversions of perception; perversions of view; [the thought] "it is not mine"—this is the perversion of perception.
The two perversions of mind; the perversion of view, [thinking] the impure is pure; and the perversion of perception.
This is the perversion of mind and the perversion of view. Furthermore, is it not the case that just as the cloth is, so is the dye; likewise, such is the awakening and such is the mind?
Oṃ, homage to the Triple Gem! At that time, the Blessed One was teaching the Perfection of Wisdom in the city of Rājagṛha to those who were not yet established in the Mahāyāna.

In the presence of a bodhisattva who has been well-instructed and is firmly established in the irreversible stage.
They are to be spoken and taught; they are not merely the emptiness of the conditioned.

They are to be spoken and taught; it is not merely the emptiness of the conditioned.

They should be spoken and taught; it is not merely emptiness that is without beginning or end.
In the presence of a bodhisattva who has been instructed in the unsurpassed and non-abiding [path].
They are to be spoken and taught; it is not merely the emptiness of non-existence.
In the presence of a bodhisattva who has been instructed in the unsurpassed and non-abiding [path].
They are to be spoken and taught; it is not merely intrinsic emptiness itself.
In the presence of a bodhisattva who has been well-instructed and is firmly established in the vehicle.
They are to be spoken and taught; it is not merely the emptiness of all phenomena.
In the presence of a bodhisattva who has been well-instructed and is firmly established in the irreversible stage.

They should be spoken and taught. It is not merely the emptiness of self-protection that is taught; rather, it is for the sake of a bodhisattva who stands firm in the non-dual [path] before one who has been thus instructed.
They are to be spoken and taught; it is not merely the emptiness of non-apprehension.
In the presence of a bodhisattva who has been well-instructed and is firmly established in the irreversible stage.
They are to be spoken of and taught; it is not the emptiness of non-existence alone.
In the presence of a bodhisattva who has been well-instructed and is firmly established in the vehicle.
They are to be spoken and taught; it is not emptiness of intrinsic nature itself.
In the presence of a bodhisattva who has been instructed in the unsurpassed and who is firmly established therein.
They are to be spoken of and taught; the faculties are not thus.
In the presence of a bodhisattva who has been instructed and is firmly established in the unsurpassed vehicle.
They are to be spoken and taught; they are not merely powers. For one who has been taught these factors and does not waver or remain unstable [in them].
They should be spoken and taught in the presence of a bodhisattva.
It is not that they do not lead to awakening; rather, it is for one who does not correctly abide in what has been taught as the non-limbs [of awakening].
In the presence of a bodhisattva, one should speak and teach nothing other than the Noble Eightfold Path.
In the presence of a bodhisattva who has been instructed in the unsurpassed and non-abiding [path].

They are to be spoken and taught; yet they are not merely the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid).

In the presence of a bodhisattva who is established in the unsurpassed vehicle as taught [by the Buddha].

In the presence of a bodhisattva who is established in the unsurpassed vehicle as taught [by the Buddha].

The root of his roots of merit has been planted; this is for one who has attended upon many Buddhas.
The perfection of wisdom itself has been taught for one who is established in the single vehicle.

In the presence of the Bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these mantras] should be recited and taught.

In the presence of the Bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these mantras] should be recited and taught.
Its nature is simply the emptiness of the ultimate truth.
In the presence of a bodhisattva who is established in the unsurpassed vehicle as taught [by the Buddha].

For him who is not established in the three vehicles as taught, there is only the emptiness of the conditioned.
In the presence of a bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [this] should be spoken and taught.
For him who is established in the single vehicle, only the emptiness of the unconditioned has been taught.
In the presence of a bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these mantras] should be recited and taught.
For one who is not established in the previously taught Mahāyāna, there is only absolute emptiness.
In the presence of the Bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these mantras] should be recited and taught.
For one who is not established in the three vehicles, as taught, the very emptiness of that [nature] is without beginning or end.
In the presence of the Bodhisattva; in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā.
They should be spoken and taught.
For him who is not established in the vehicle that was taught, there is indeed the emptiness of non-dispersal.
In the presence of the Bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these mantras] should be recited and taught.
For him who is established in the well-taught Mahāyāna, there is only the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
In the presence of a bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these mantras] should be spoken and taught.
For him who is established in the single vehicle, the emptiness of all phenomena alone has been taught.

For him who is established in the Mahāyāna as taught, there is only the emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*).
In the presence of the Bodhisattva; in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā.
They should be spoken and taught.
For one who is not established in the three vehicles, the emptiness of non-apprehension of that [object] has been taught.
In the presence of the Bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these mantras] should be recited and taught.
For him who is established in the Mahāyāna as taught, there is indeed the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
In the presence of the Bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these mantras] should be recited and taught.
For him who is established in the supreme vehicle as taught, there is only the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
In the presence of the Bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these mantras] should be recited and taught.
For one who is not yet established in the Mahāyāna, only the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence has been taught.
In the presence of the Bodhisattva.

For him who is firmly established in the Great Vehicle as taught, the very foundations of mindfulness [are the means].
In the presence of the Bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these mantras] should be recited and taught.

In the presence of the Bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [this] should be spoken and taught.
In the presence of that very Bodhisattva who has been established in the vehicles taught by him,
and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā.
They should be spoken and taught.
His very powers were taught to him as he stood present before the Bodhisattva.
It should be spoken and taught in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā.
For him who is established in the Mahāyāna as taught by the one born from the family of awakening, it is indeed [the case].
It should be recited and taught in the presence of a bodhisattva and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā.
For him who has been established in the single vehicle, the Noble Eightfold Path has been taught.
In the presence of a bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [this] should be spoken and taught.

In the presence of the Bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [this] should be spoken and taught.
For him who is established in the well-taught and unsurpassed vehicles, there are indeed the meditative absorptions (dhyānas).
In the presence of the Bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these mantras] should be recited and taught.
For him who has correctly established himself in the vehicle taught by the Immeasurables, there are indeed the Immeasurables themselves.
In the presence of the Bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these mantras] should be recited and taught.
For one who has not yet entered into the meditative attainments of the formless realm as they have been taught, [there is no attainment].
In the presence of a bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [this] should be spoken and taught.
For him who is established in the single vehicle as taught, there are indeed eight liberations.
In the presence of a bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [this] should be spoken and taught.
These are precisely the successive attainments of meditative dwelling.
In the presence of a bodhisattva who is established in the supreme vehicle as taught by the Teacher.
In the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these] should be spoken and taught.
To him who has been established in the single vehicle, having been taught the gateways to liberation— emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—
in the presence of a bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā.

These very supernormal knowledges were taught for the sake of the Bodhisattva who was established in the unsurpassed vehicle and stood before him.
In the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these] should be spoken and taught.
For him who, through that very concentration, has been instructed and is established in the vehicle of no-more-learning (anavayāna).
In the presence of a bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these mantras] should be recited and taught.
For him who has been established in the true vehicle, the very gateways of the dhāraṇīs have been taught.
In the presence of a bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these mantras] should be recited and taught.
For him who is established in the single vehicle as taught by the Tathāgata, there are indeed the ten powers of a Tathāgata.
In the presence of a bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these mantras] should be recited and taught.
He possesses the four grounds of self-confidence for one who is firmly established in the well-taught, unerring vehicle.
In the presence of a bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these mantras] should be spoken and taught.
For him who is well-established in the single vehicle, the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid) have indeed been taught.
In the presence of the Bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these mantras] should be spoken and taught.
For him, there are indeed eighteen unconditioned qualities of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha.
In the presence of a bodhisattva who is established in the unsurpassed vehicle as taught [by the Buddha].
In the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these] should be spoken and taught.
This very omniscience should be spoken and taught in the presence of a bodhisattva who is established in the Mahāyāna and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā.
For him who has not yet established himself in the single vehicle (ekayāna), it is precisely the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) that has been taught.
In the presence of the Bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these mantras] should be recited and taught.
For one who has not yet established themselves in the Great Vehicle, only omniscience itself has been taught.
In the presence of a bodhisattva, and in the presence of Mahāpratyamgirā, [these mantras] should be recited and taught.
Her conqueror is the Great Pratyamgirā, the Queen of Great Vidyās. Listen, O Bodhisattva!
The Great Being, having shared this meritorious basis associated with sympathetic joy together with all sentient beings, dedicates it toward unexcelled, perfect,
and complete enlightenment.

And that is by way of non-apprehension. And this is the basis of meritorious action accompanied by rejoicing for all sentient beings, as well as for those belonging to the vehicle of the śrāvakas and those belonging to the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas.

The basis of meritorious action consisting of giving; the basis of meritorious action consisting of ethical discipline; and the basis of meritorious action consisting of meditation—this is the basis of meritorious action associated with rejoicing belonging to the bodhisattva. Having made it common to all sentient beings together, [he dedicates it] toward supreme...
That which has been dedicated toward perfect enlightenment is said to be a thousandfold.
It is called the eldest; it is called the best; it is called the most excellent.
It is described as sublime; it is described as unsurpassed; it is described as peerless.
It is called "unequal. It is called "equal to the unequal. For what reason?
This is the Aparājitā named Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣa-śītāntapattrā.
Mahāpratyaṅgirā, the Queen of Great Vidyās; likewise, for those belonging to the vehicles of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, there is the basis of meritorious action consisting of generosity.
O unshakable one, O uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas, O cool-leaved one! O great Pratyamgirā!

Thus, by means of the glorious Buddhayoga, the recitation of the Pūtrī mantra must be performed during all calamities.

and gandharvas, O Lord, rejoiced exceedingly at what was spoken by the Blessed Vajrasattva Mañjuśrī.
Thus, in the noble *Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣa-śītāntapattrā*, from the *Dvādaśasāhasrikā*.
In the *Mahāpratyamgirā*, in the *Mahāvidyārājñī*, and in the *Lokālokā*.
In the Mahāpratyamgirā, the Treatise on the Instruction of Dharma, O you whose Dharma-body is perfectly pure!
The embodiment of wisdom, spoken by the great Mañjuśrī, Lord of Speech; the ultimate reality; established through the unsurpassed teaching of the Dharma; emerged from names; the Great Pratyamgirā.
The Great Queen of Spells. Upon the head of Avalokita. The completion of the third kalpa.
Auspiciousness!

There is a circle of water devoid of waves, wherein lies the circle of the garland of jewels; first, there is the golden lotus of the virtuous, whose abode is among the holy. Upon that is the jewel-lotus, the abode of the moon-like flowers, which has brought benefit to the world. [This is] the glorious *Mahāpratyaṅgirā* of the thousand-fold Śāha.
The Blessed Ladies, whose essence is the five primordial Buddhas; who are skilled in the fourfold destruction of the thousand-fold world-systems;
whose minds encompass thousands of millions; and who, in a mere moment, [purify] the abodes of the Buddhas across multitudes of thousands, tens of thousands, and millions of worlds.
I perpetually bow to her who possesses a voice of sovereign lordship over a thousand worlds, she who is the universal form.
"Of those phenomena which arise from a cause, the Tathāgata has stated their cause, as well as their cessation;
such is the teaching of the Great Śramaṇa."
May there be auspiciousness at all times for the welfare of sons and grandsons.

They have not acted falsely toward me; they have not been devoid of wisdom. Through austerity, they have attained the state of Ajimāmanimayajuḥ, [and have reached] Ajimā (2) Piṇḍakalya.
This is the power of the glorious Mahāpratyaṅgirā, which leads one to the beautiful and auspicious Sukhāvatī.

May the glorious Mahāvairocana, Vajrasattva, and the Guru Śrī Mahāmañjuśrī grant their gracious vision. May they cause these lineages to endure and expand the continuity of the family. [May they grant] birth, wealth, happiness, and fame.
May the multitude of virtues, which bestows long life and freedom from disease, increase for those who possess them. || 4 ||
